title: Support fontName in textMateRules
Have a history for recently edited editors
body:
It seems the following 2 features are missing from vscode:

1. a dedicated list for recently **edited** files, excluding the files opened only for readonly view
2. recent **edit positions**, an action to jump back to recent cursor positions where changes were done, should support jumping through multiple files.

When working on a project with lots of files, one might need to jump through many files, but only edit a few, the list of *recent files* could help but it would be great to have a dedicated action to list only **recently edited files**, and to navigate through them.

And jumping back to previous edit positions allows one to be right back on the spot, immediately, to resume previous work when briefly interrupted for API lookup or similar things, thus it would be very helpful for one to be able to navigate through the places where modifications has been done recently.

For reference, such features already exist in IntelliJ IDEA, see: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/pycharm/navigating-to-recent-file.html

- VSCode Version: 1.19.3
- OS Version: macOS 10.13

title: Add wordwrap indicator
body:
There's currently no visual indication when you use the `"editor.wordWrap": "on"` setting.

I'd propose optionally adding a wordwrap-indicator on each newline, something like this: 

so it becomes easy to spot when a line has been wordwrapped.

title: Add a setting to always show sidebar even when opening empty window
body: It would be great if we had an option to always show the sidebar on startup, even if opening with just one file. Have a consistent user interface, rather than one that moves around depending on the number of files open is important to some of us.

title: VSCode should follow .lnk
body:
VSCode should be able to resolve `.lnk` files, if this link leads to a file on the users hard drive.
Thus the user can open the file right away by clicking on the link file in the sidebar.

title: Debug console: introduce ctrl + up / down to focus output
body:
To be consistent with the terminal the debug console could also navigte to output using ctrl + up / down.
The current functionality of Shit + Tab, and up / down would still work as it is today, and ctrl + up / down would behave like an alias of sort.

title: Detached DOM nodes memory leak
body: The Edge Dev Tools now offers Detached Elements tool to help detect memory leaks. The tool is a good addition to the memory heap tool but it's analyzing from a different angle. @sbatten and I spent some time digging into this tool and fixed memory leaks in the `ActionBar` successfully. Here is how we tackle the leaks in action bar: * Open vscode (`scripts/code-web.sh`) in Edge * Play around with it for a bit * Open Edge Dev Tools -> `...` -> `More Tools` -> `Detached Elements` * Click the trash icon to trigger manual GC and click the first button to collect all detached elements * It found 100+ detached elements which can not be GC'ed. We easily found dozens of `markers-panel-action-filter-container` * To analyze why they can't be GC'ed, click the Eye icon on the top toolbar to generate a heap dump * Once the memory heap is generated, it will link the detached element to the objects in the memory tool Turned out we register a global DOM listener for every `ActionViewItem` and store it in `ActionBar` disposable store. When the `ActionViewItem` is disposed, the DOM listener will be not disposed/cleared until the `ActionBar` is disposed. --- With the `ActionBar` leaks fixed, there are still 30+ detached DOM nodes not GC'ed. Not every one is necessarily memory leak (for example, if you are using `ListView`, it will hold refs to template DOM nodes) but some of them are duplicated elements. - [x] Multiple `markers-panel-action-filter-container` and `switch-output` @sbatten - [x] Multiple `status.languageStatus` span and `codicon codicon-bracket wiggle` span nodes are ref'ed by mutation observers in `SuggestDetailsOverlay` @jrieken - [x] DOM node for monaco editor in `AccessibilityHelpWidget` @isidorn

title: [css] Add new CSS color functions
body:
[CSS Color Modules 4](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/) added many new color functions. This spec already Candidate Recommendation Draft and was implemented in Safari 15 without any flags. We already have a few articles about the most interesting of them [`oklch()`](https://evilmartians.com/chronicles/oklch-in-css-why-quit-rgb-hsl) and [`lch()`](https://lea.verou.me/2020/04/lch-colors-in-css-what-why-and-how/).

We need the same color preview box as we have for other colors like `red`.

Functions:
* [`oklch()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/oklch) and [`oklab()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/oklab)
* [`lch()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/lch) and [`lab()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/lab)

title: [json] formatter: option to keep object in arrays on the same line
Allow display prop on markdown span style
body:
Style attribute added to span tags in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/97793
Currently, it allows setting `color` and `background-color` but many times the background color doesn't apply because span is `display: inline` by default and doesn't have an actual width and height.
Adding `display` prop to the allowed styles will fix that and also will open up many other (safe) options for layoutting.

e.g, in [pretty-ts-errors](https://github.com/yoavbls/pretty-ts-errors) I had to use codicon classes to apply background-color and make things inlined. That classes bring unwanted styles like `user-select: none` that prevent selecting and copying the content.
Now it's a huge deal for tens of thousands of developers that can't copy the types from their errors.

I know that no one wants to keep adding styles to the sanitized regex and it opens the barrier for other requests like this but `display` prop is different. It is not a niche CSS prop, it is one of the most essential props in CSS and one of the few things that markdown can't do.
  
**I made a pull request that add it, I hope it helps: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/180498**

title: Improve box select / multi-cursor editing - expose `editor.emptySelectionClipboard` as keybinding
body:
### Scenario and Problem

 * i like the feature of being able to cut/copy current line without any selection i.e. the setting `editor.emptySelectionClipboard`
 * but i don't like the fact that it uses the same keybind as copy-selection i.e. `editor.action.clipboard{Cut,Copy}Action`

**problem:**

* this often results in important data from clipboard getting accidentally overwritten and hence, lost

* this makes box or column select mode useless to select & cut some part, where some line in between doesn't have content in that part

  https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8666831e-7552-40f5-afad-48bc574ffad1

* this is so grave that i am forced to disable this `editor.emptySelectionClipboard` altogether for the time being

so, having ability to pick a separate dedicated keybind for `editor.emptySelectionClipboard` will help a lot.

### Verbose/Detailed Wording:

* i want `CTRL-c` to work only when there is some selection
* i don't want `CTRL-c` to copy anything on empty selection
* i want to use the feature of "copy current line on empty selection" with some other keybind 
* but that other keybind or its event should NOT be inherently coupled to the normal "copy-selection" feature

### Versions

```yaml
Version: 1.88.1
Release: 24104
Commit: 0d01a72525276e5e3771fe5851b9c83de0de1e2b
Date: 2024-04-13T01:53:59.491Z

ElectronBuildId: undefined
Chromium: 120.0.6099.291
Node.js: 18.18.2
V8: 12.0.267.19-electron.0
OS: Linux x64 6.6.44
```

### existing issues showing problematic nature of this "feature"

* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/135006 by @shaozi

### old titles of this issue:

* Improve box select - expose Empty Selection Clipboard as keybinding
* expose Empty Selection Clipboard as a dedicated keybinding
* expose `editor.emptySelectionClipboard` as a dedicated keybinding-command

title: Overriding XDG_DATA_HOME in snap leads to multiple problems
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

Version: 1.97.0-insider
Commit: 9b0b13d9bfe21c3dfd227bfaa8ed5693e309a2e0
Date: 2025-01-08T05:06:32.681Z
Electron: 32.2.7
ElectronBuildId: 10660205
Chromium: 128.0.6613.186
Node.js: 20.18.1
V8: 12.8.374.38-electron.0
OS: Linux x64 6.12.8-1-MANJARO snap

2d28c0a79c87 added a feature that redefines `XDG_DATA_HOME` to be `$SNAP_USER_DATA/.local/share`. This leads to several problems

- This creates a bogus Trash that's not the system one, and as such is unmanageable (and is carried over from update to update, gradually inflating) : #233649, #237147 
- Since it also applies to commands run in the integrated terminal, all programs that use XDG dirs will only see the local snap ones instead of the system ones. E.g. :
  - Messing up fish (#232741) and Xonsh histories
  - Creates a separate brittle data dir for uv (what lead me here)
  - Creates a separate root for virtualenvwrapper, with environments created outside vscode not accessible inside and vice-versa
  - Probably many other subtle and hard to track bugs

Would it be possible to revert this, or at least have an option to make it opt-out-able?

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.99.2
- OS Version: Linux, Ubuntu 24.10, Wayland session

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VSCode in a Wayland session, either in native Wayland mode (with flag --ozone-platform=wayland) or in the default XWayland mode
2. Drag and drop a file from the Explorer into the current editor, and hold the Shift key
3. The file is not dropped into the current editor, instead it is opened in a new editor tab, as if Shift were not pressed.

Demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/049287d6-07a9-4fdf-b2ff-4780bcf27e19

Expected behavior, when using an X11 desktop session instead of Wayland:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca0d251f-80f8-4bc9-9263-0abf016bbac6

I have tested this on both Ubuntu and Fedora, and the bug consistently appears in both. 
I have also tested older versions (such as 1.92, 1.91, 1.92, 1.68) and the problem was already present.

title: Images from private repositories not loaded in markdown preview
body:
## Description:

When you use an GitHub image reference into a Markdown file like: `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39942c49-500f-4f26-b6c2-a08fbddbbb0b` it’s uploaded as a private-repo asset and renders perfectly in GitHub’s preview. But in VS Code, those images break because the preview pane doesn’t authenticate to fetch private assets.

## Steps to Reproduce:

On GitHub.com, open or create a Markdown (.md) file in a private repository.

1. Paste an image via Ctrl+V—GitHub uploads it and inserts a link like:
   ```md
   
   ```
1. Commit your changes.
1. In GitHub.com’s own preview, the image displays correctly.
1. Clone/open the repo in VS Code (or open it on github.dev) and launch the built-in Markdown preview.
1. Observe: the image link returns 404/unauthorized and fails to load.

## Expected Behavior:
VS Code should reuse your GitHub credentials (session or PAT) in the Markdown preview so that private-repo assets load seamlessly.

## Actual Behavior:
Preview fetches asset URLs without auth headers, resulting in broken images.

## Proposed Solutions:

- Authenticate the preview pane using your GitHub session or a user-provided token.
- Cache pasted assets locally and fallback to the local file if remote fetch fails.
- Add a setting for supplying a Personal Access Token for private-repo asset access.

title: .gitignore respected in a multi root workspace.
body:
When a `.gitignore` is defined in a standard workspace VS code explorer automatically hides all matching files, however in a multi root workspace this only works for the root workspace and others it doesn't.

The only workaround currently is to manually replicate rules form `.gitignore` into `"settings": { "files.exclude": [] }` in the workspace file, which is fragile as everyone needs to remember to update both files when making changes.

Ideally having all workspaces apply the setting would be the default but any option to have this enabled would be great.

title: Model of a custom editor URI is never cleared
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.100.3 (although this probably happens in all versions)
- OS Version: Windows 10

Steps to Reproduce:

1. With a custom editor implementation, invoke `vscode.commands.executeCommand("vscode.openWith", uri, CustomEditorProvider.viewType)`
2. Throw an `Error` from `CustomEditorProvider.openCustomDocument`
3. Close the opened tab with the VS Code error message and the "Try Again" button
4. Step 1 again

VS Code seems to cache the custom editor model by URI, never discarding it.

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/519df4f08646561bc1fc6b142dab9d80c1bf225c/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.ts#L164-L170

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/519df4f08646561bc1fc6b142dab9d80c1bf225c/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.ts#L239-L242

That means await-ing `existingModel` will re-throw the same `Error` over and over again.

title: Copilot “Manage Models...” option not shown when VSCode itself is using a `socks5h` proxy
body: Screenshot: - Copilot Chat Extension Version: 1.372.0 - VS Code Version: 1.104.1 (Universal) - OS Version: macOS 26.0 - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Model picker (`Manage Models...` option) - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): 3rd-party model via [extension that implemented `LanguageModelChatProvider` support](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=johnny-zhao.oai-compatible-copilot) - Logs: how can I get the log? Steps to Reproduce: 1. Set vscode's proxy setting to a valid socks5h proxy endpoint (e.g. `"http.proxy": "socks5h://127.0.0.1:8888"`) 2. Reload VSCode workspace 3. Open Copilot chat panel, wait for the model picker area to appear 4. See result: model picker appears, have a list of models but at the bottom of the list, there is no `Manage Models...` option. 5. Change the `http.proxy` setting value's protocol from `socks5h://` to `socks5://`, and then repeat step 2 and 3 6. See result: model picker appears, with `Manage Models...` option available at the end of the list. Additional info: 1. I am using Copilot Free, and intended to use 3rd-party API provider via the extension that mentioned above. 2. I *personally* think `Manage Models...` entry should always be available, especially when the user intentionally wants to use 3rd-party model provider instead of GitHub Copilot's first party models... Let me know if you need any additional information. Thanks!

title: Feature request: Configurable reasoning level and “max context” mode in VS Code Copilot Chat
body: Summary Please add the ability in VS Code Copilot Chat to (1) explicitly select the reasoning level used by the model and (2) enable a “max” mode that uses the largest possible context window for that model. Problem Right now, when using Copilot Chat in VS Code, it is not clear: What reasoning level (standard vs. higher / advanced reasoning) is actually being used for a given chat. How much of the project context the model can see or is allowed to use in a given conversation. This makes it hard to decide when Copilot Chat is suitable for deeper, multi-step tasks (large refactors, architecture reviews, complex debugging, etc.). For long or complex requests, answers often get cut off or simplified, and it’s unclear whether that’s due to reasoning limits, context limits, or both. Other tools in the market (for example, Cursor) already expose controls to choose a reasoning level and a “max” or “deep” mode. Having something similar in VS Code Copilot Chat would give users more control and predictability. Proposed solution Expose a “Reasoning level” control Allow users to select, per conversation (and/or globally), something like: Fast / standard Balanced Deep / high reasoning Show somewhere in the UI which level is currently active so the user always knows what they are paying for and what to expect in terms of depth. Add a “Max context” mode per model Provide an optional “Max context” toggle or mode that: Uses the largest context window available for the selected model. Is clearly labeled as more resource-intensive / potentially slower. When “Max context” is enabled, make it explicit in the UI (badge or label) so users know the assistant is allowed to read and use as much context as possible (files, history, etc.) for that model. Configuration surface A simple UI in the Copilot Chat panel (dropdowns, toggles). Optionally, support in settings.json or agent configuration so teams can set: Default reasoning level. Whether “Max context” is allowed or enforced for specific workflows. Benefits Transparency: Users always know what reasoning level and context mode are being applied. Better control for complex tasks: For deep code reviews, architecture changes, or large refactors, users can explicitly choose a “deep reasoning + max context” setup instead of guessing. Predictable behavior across tools: Brings VS Code Copilot Chat closer to other AI-enhanced editors that already expose reasoning/context controls, making it easier for teams to standardize workflows. Improved user trust: When responses are truncated or simplified, users can understand whether it’s due to the chosen mode rather than assuming a limitation or a bug. Additional notes Even if the default behavior remains “automatic” (Copilot chooses reasoning and context usage), it would be extremely valuable to: Expose which mode is currently being used. Give power users an explicit way to switch to higher reasoning and max context when needed.

title: Gemini Pro 3: Server error. Stream terminated when used after other models in the same conversation
body:
# Issue: Gemini Pro 3 returns `Server error. Stream terminated` when used after other models in same conversation

## Summary
When using **Gemini Pro 3** in VS Code Copilot Chat, the model frequently stops mid-response and shows the error:

**Server error. Stream terminated**

This only occurs when the conversation includes previous messages from **other models** (e.g., GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus).  
When starting a **new chat with no prior context**, Gemini Pro 3 works normally.

This suggests an issue with **mixed-model conversation context** or **model switching within a thread**.

---

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open VS Code Copilot Chat.
2. Start a long conversation using another model (e.g., GPT-5.1, Sonnet 4.5).

title: Skills: Dynamic context injection (shell command preprocessing in prompt files)
body:
## Follow-up to #285172

Now that SKILL.md files are invocable as `/commands`, a natural next step is **dynamic context injection** — the ability to run shell commands at invocation time and inject their output into the prompt before it reaches the model.

Spec issue: https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/issues/124

### Problem

Today, prompt files (`.prompt.md`) and skills (`SKILL.md`) are static text. Users who want to include live data — like git diffs, PR details, environment info, or build status — must either:
- Manually paste it into the chat alongside the `/command`
- Write a separate script and copy output

This makes skills less useful for deployment, review, and CI-related workflows.

### Proposed behavior

Support a preprocessing syntax (e.g. `` !`command` ``) in the prompt body that executes a shell command and replaces the placeholder with its output before the prompt is sent to the model.

Example `SKILL.md`:
```markdown
---
name: pr-summary
description: Summarize changes in the current pull request
---

## Pull request context
- PR diff: !`gh pr diff`
- PR comments: !`gh pr view --comments`
- Changed files: !`gh pr diff --name-only`

## Your task
Summarize this pull request focusing on breaking changes and test coverage.
```

When invoked via `/pr-summary`, the shell commands run first and their stdout replaces each placeholder. The model only sees the fully-rendered prompt with actual data.

### Prior art

- [Claude Code skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) support this via `` !`command` `` syntax
- [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io) (adopted by VS Code) includes dynamic context as a feature

### Security considerations

- Commands should respect the same trust/permission model as terminal execution
- Workspace trust should gate command execution
- Failed commands should surface clearly (not silently omit output)
- Consider a timeout for long-running commands

title: Add `model` field to Copilot agent hook inputs
body:
## Feature Request

### Problem

VS Code Copilot agent hooks (introduced in v1.109) do not include the active model name in any hook's input payload. The common fields sent to all hooks are:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "...",
  "cwd": "...",
  "sessionId": "...",
  "hookEventName": "...",
  "transcript_path": "..."
}
```
Event-specific hooks like UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and PostToolUse also lack a model identifier.

Use Case
Security and policy enforcement tools (e.g., extensions that enforce model allow/deny lists) need to know which model is active at hook time in order to:
* Block disallowed models before a prompt is sent (UserPromptSubmit)
* Audit which model was used for each tool call (PreToolUse / PostToolUse)
* Enforce organizational policies that restrict usage to approved models

Without the model name in the hook input, model-based policy enforcement is impossible. Reading transcript_path is a fragile workaround since its format is undocumented.

Claude Code hooks already include a model field in their inputs, so this would bring VS Code hooks to parity.

Proposed Solution
Add a model field to the common hook input fields sent to all hook events:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "...",
  "cwd": "...",
  "sessionId": "...",
  "hookEventName": "...",
  "transcript_path": "...",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-5"
}
```

Additional Context
Aligns with the Claude Code hooks spec which already includes model in hook inputs
Requested by extension developers building security/compliance tooling on top of VS Code agent hooks

title: Non-workspace skill resource files (personal & plugin) not accessible to search tools (grep_search, file_search, semantic_search)
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.39.0
- VS Code Version: 1.111.0 (ce099c1ed25d9eb3076c11e4a280f3eb52b4fbeb, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 10
- Feature: Agent mode (Skills)
- Selected model: Claude Opus 4.6
- Logs: N/A

## Summary

When a Skill (`SKILL.md`) installed via a **plugin** (`chat.pluginLocations`) is activated, its companion resource files (referenced via relative paths like `./docs/reference.txt`) are not accessible to workspace-scoped search tools. Only `read_file` works (via absolute path). This limits the agent's ability to efficiently look up information in the skill's own reference files.

> **Note:** This issue is specific to skills installed via plugins, where the skill directory lives outside the current workspace. Skills placed inside the workspace (e.g., `.github/skills/`) do not have this problem because their files are already workspace-scoped.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a custom Skill with a `SKILL.md` that references sibling resource files (e.g., `[reference.txt](./docs/reference.txt)`)
2. Install the skill via a plugin registered in `chat.pluginLocations` (i.e., the skill directory is outside the workspace)
3. Activate the skill in a Copilot Chat agent conversation
4. Observe that `read_file` succeeds on the skill's resource files using the absolute path
5. Observe that `grep_search`, `file_search`, and `semantic_search` all fail to find or search those same files — they are workspace-scoped and the plugin's skill directory is not included

## Expected Behavior

When a plugin-installed Skill is activated, the skill's directory (and subdirectories) should be included in the search scope for read-only tools (`grep_search`, `file_search`, `semantic_search`), since the skill system already resolves the absolute path to serve the SKILL.md content. The skill declaration implies trust in these files.

## Actual Behavior

| Tool | Can access plugin skill resources? |
|------|-----|
| read_file | Yes (absolute path) |
| grep_search | No — workspace-scoped only |
| file_search | No — workspace-scoped only |
| semantic_search | No — workspace-scoped only |

## Impact

Skills that include large reference files (e.g., a 2,500-line API reference) are significantly less useful because the agent cannot search them — it must read large sections and scan manually, or fall back to terminal commands as a workaround. This disproportionately affects plugin-installed skills, which are specifically designed to be reusable across workspaces.

## Related

This is related to #293386 (`additionalReadAccessPaths`), which provides a manual workaround. However:
1. That setting would require users to manually configure paths for every skill — skills already declare their file location
2. Automatic inclusion of skill resource directories is the natural solution

title: Agent Skills: only first 21 skills are invokable via skill() despite prompt advertising more
body:
## Summary

GitHub Copilot Chat advertises additional Agent Skills as being invokable via the `skill()` tool, but **only the first 21 skills expanded as full `<skill>` blocks in the system prompt are actually registered**. Skills listed under **“Additional skills available (invoke by name)”** are **not callable** and always fail with `Skill '<name>' not found`.

This affects **both the main agent and subagents** and appears to be caused by a hard cap (likely token‑budget related) on how many skills are fully materialized.

---

## Expected behavior

Any skill listed in the system prompt under:

> **Additional skills available (invoke by name)**

should be callable via:

```text
skill("<skill-name>")
```

as advertised by the system prompt.

---

## Actual behavior

Only skills that appear as **fully described `<skill>` blocks** (with description and file path) in the system prompt are registered with the `skill()` tool.

All other skills listed by name only result in a hard failure:

```text
Skill '<skill-name>' not found.
Available skills: [list of ~21 skills]
```

This happens consistently and deterministically.

---

## Observed data

| Metric | Count |
|------|------|
| Skills discovered (Skill Discovery event) | **63** |
| Skills rendered as full `<skill>` blocks | **21** |
| Skills listed as “Additional skills available (invoke by name)” | **42** |
| Skills actually callable via `skill()` | **21** |

The cutoff is alphabetical:

- ✅ `figma-create-design-system-rules` (#21) — works  
- ❌ `figma-create-new-file` (#22) — listed as “additional”, but fails  

This strongly suggests a **hard cap at 21 skills**, likely due to system‑prompt token budgeting.

---

## Reproduction steps

1. Configure a workspace with **more than 21 Agent Skills** (project or personal).
2. Ensure skills are alphabetically ordered.
3. Start Copilot Chat (agent mode).
4. Inspect the system prompt:
   - The first ~21 skills appear as full `<skill>` blocks.
   - Remaining skills appear under **“Additional skills available (invoke by name)”**.
5. Attempt to invoke any “additional” skill:

```text
skill("react-development")
```

6. Observe the error:

```text
Skill 'react-development' not found.
Available skills: [only the first 21]
```

---

## Scope clarification

- ❌ **Not subagent‑specific**
- ✅ Reproduces identically in:
  - the main agent
  - subagents
- Subagents made the issue more visible because they followed `AGENTS.md` instructions literally and attempted to load skills that were advertised but not registered.

---

## Workarounds

- Rename important skills so they sort into the **top 21 alphabetically**.
- Bypass `skill()` entirely and have agents read `SKILL.md` directly via `read_file`.

Both approaches are brittle and unintended.

---

## Why this is a bug

The system prompt explicitly instructs agents to load **all listed skills by name**, but the `skill()` tool enforces a hidden whitelist limited to the subset expanded as full blocks.

This is a **prompt / tool contract violation**:
- The prompt claims certain skills are callable.
- The tool rejects them unconditionally.

At minimum, the prompt should not advertise skills that the tool cannot load.

---

## Suggested fixes (non‑prescriptive)

- Ensure all discovered skills listed as invokable are registered with `skill()`, **or**
- Remove or reword the **“Additional skills available (invoke by name)”** section, **or**
- Make the cap explicit and documented, **or**
- Allow lazy loading of skills b

title: MCP Registry "Registry only" enforcement blocks all servers even when they exist in the registry
body:
Type: Bug 1.) Configure MCP registry URL in org Copilot admin settings (tested with both a custom registry and the official https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) 2.) Set "Restrict MCP access to registry servers" to "Registry only" 3.) Configure an MCP server in mcp.json with a name that exists in the registry (e.g. io.github.upstash/context7 which is confirmed in the official registry) 4.) Reload VS Code Expected Behavior Servers whose names match entries in the configured registry should be enabled/allowed. Actual Behavior All MCP servers show as disabled with the message: "This MCP Server is disabled because it is configured to be disabled in the Editor. Please check your settings." Diagnostic Findings Using Developer Tools → Network tab, I confirmed: VS Code fetches mcp_registry and receives a 200 with the correct registry URL and "registry_access": "registry_only" VS Code fetches servers?limit=1 and gets a valid response from the registry However, VS Code only fetches one page (limit=1) and does not query for specific server names — so unless the server happens to be on that first page, it's never found Additional Context Switching to "Allow all" immediately restores all MCP servers (no restart needed) Tested with the official MCP registry (https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) — same result The server io.github.upstash/context7 is confirmed to exist in the official registry via browser The servers?limit=1 request only returns the first alphabetical entry (ac.inference.sh/mcp), never my actual server I also tried with my own mcp registry which returns the below. Same problem occurs as described above https://mcp-registry-service.onrender.com/v0.1/servers VS Code version: Code - Insiders 1.120.0-insider (07ef5b69ded08bde157121ece4a640c085c836a3, 2026-05-07T12:59:32+02:00) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100 Modes:

title: vscode and voice over mac os
body:
Hello,
When I use VS Code on macOS 26, I encounter several accessibility issues.
The most significant issue is a synchronization problem between the braille display and the VoiceOver cursor. The text displayed under the VoiceOver cursor does not match the text shown on the braille display, which makes it very difficult to work efficiently.
I tried updating the accessibility settings in VS Code, but the issue remains. I experience this problem with every type of file, including .txt, .js, .php, and .py files.
When I navigate through the sidebar to browse files and folders, I see "groups" displayed on my braille display. The same issue occurs in the console when I try to read error messages.
Thank you for looking into this issue.

title: Block auto-approval of file-write redirection to ~ and % paths
body:
Extends the file-write redirection guard to also block auto-approval when the destination path contains `~` (POSIX tilde expansion) or `%` (Windows env-var expansion), since neither `posix.isAbsolute` nor `win32.isAbsolute` classifies these as absolute paths.

Adds regression tests for both bash (`~/file.txt`, `%HOME%/file.txt`) and pwsh (`~\file.txt`, `%APPDATA%\file.txt`).

Tracking internal PR: devdiv-microsoft/vscode-private#43

title: AGENTS.md discovery still runs `rg --no-ignore --follow` over the whole tree (regression sibling of #304676)
body:
### Environment
| Component | Value |
| VS Code | 1.126.0 |
| OS | macOS (Darwin arm64, Apple Silicon) |
| Workspace | pnpm monorepo, large `node_modules` with 200+ top-level symlinks + `.pnpm` store |
| Related (fixed) issue | #304676 (shipped 1.116.0) |

### Summary
#304676 fixed the `.github/agents/*.md` scan (scoped it to the `.github/agents/` folder, shipped in 1.116). But the **`AGENTS.md` instruction-file discovery** is a separate scan that still uses the same `--no-ignore --follow` flags and still walks the entire workspace, including all of `node_modules`. On a large pnpm monorepo this pins CPU (490-871%), respawns every few seconds, and heats the machine while VS Code is idle.

### The command being run
.../@vscode/ripgrep-universal/bin/darwin-arm64/rg --files --hidden --case-sensitive --no-require-git -g /AGENTS.md -g !/.git -g !/.svn -g !/.hg -g !/.DS_Store -g !/Thumbs.db --no-ignore --follow --no-config --no-ignore-global
Note the glob is `**/AGENTS.md`, not `/.github/agents/*.md` - this is the instruction-file path, not the agent-definitions path that #304676 patched.
Parent process is `Code Helper (Plugin)` (the extension host).

### Workspace
pnpm monorepo, large `node_modules` with 200+ top-level symlinks + a `.pnpm` store.
Same `--follow` + pnpm symlink-forest pathology described in #304676 (file system loop errors, repeated traversal).

### Expected
Apply the same fix #304676 used: scope the AGENTS.md lookup, drop `--follow`, and/or
respect `.gitignore` so `node_modules` is skipped. Debounce instead of respawning.

### Actual
`**/AGENTS.md` scan runs with `--no-ignore --follow` across the full tree, repeatedly.

### Workaround
```jsonc
"chat.useAgentsMdFile": false,
"chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles": false,
"search.followSymlinks": false

title: Double-click selection should respect language token boundaries
body:
## Current behavior

Double-click selection appears to be based on generic word separators rather than language tokens.

For example, in JavaScript:

```js
const a = 34.8;
```

Double-clicking may select either 34 or 8 depending on which side of the decimal is clicked, even though 34.8 is a single numeric literal.

The same applies to other numeric forms:

```js
1e-6
0xff
0b1010
1_000_000
123n
```

## Expected behavior

When language tokenization is available, double-click selection should select the entire language token.

## Why `editor.wordSeparators` isn't sufficient

Changing word separator behavior globally would also affect unrelated constructs such as:

`user.profile.name`

where selecting only the clicked identifier is usually the desired behavior.

The editor already recognizes numeric literals as single tokens for syntax highlighting and other language features, so it seems reasonable for double-click selection to use the same token boundaries when available.

This could also benefit other token types where punctuation is part of a single language token (for example, regex literals or CSS color literals), but numeric literals are the clearest and most common example.

title: "Open View" quick access: filtering by container name is case-sensitive
body:
In the "Open View" quick access (run `View: Open View`, or the `view` prefix in Quick Open), an entry matches the filter if either its view label fuzzy-matches (case-insensitive) or its container label matches via `fuzzyContains(entry.containerLabel, filter)`. The container-label path is case-sensitive, so filtering by a container name only works in lowercase.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Run "View: Open View".
2. Type `explorer`. Views grouped under the Explorer container (e.g. Outline, Timeline) appear, matched by their container label.
3. Type `Explorer` (capital E, as the UI displays the container). Those entries drop out.

Expected: matching by container name is case-insensitive, so `Explorer` and `explorer` return the same views.

Actual: any uppercase character in the query fails to match the container label, so typing the container name as displayed returns fewer results than the lowercase form.

Root cause: `fuzzyContains` in `src/vs/base/common/strings.ts` lowercases the target but compares it against the original-case query characters. The other two callers (Test Explorer filter, file search) pre-lowercase the query before calling, which is why the defect only surfaces in Open View.

A fix is up at #324047.

title: Agents renderer OOM: unbounded workspaceFileCount telemetry search materializes every file
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. The direct trigger is in the core Sessions contribution, and it reproduces with two different agent providers.

- VS Code Version: 1.128.1 (`5264f2156cbcd7aea5fd004d29eaa10209155d66`), arm64
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon, 36 GB RAM
- Telemetry setting: `telemetry.telemetryLevel: "off"`
- Feature: standalone Agents/Sessions window

## Summary

Sending a foreground message in the Agents/Sessions window can start an unbounded recursive file search solely to compute the `workspaceFileCount` telemetry field. When an agent session uses a large directory as its workspace (in this reproduction, `$HOME` with approximately 1.85 million non-excluded files), every matching file URI is streamed from the extension host to the renderer and retained until the search completes. The renderer V8 heap grows by several gigabytes and terminates with an out-of-memory crash.

This also occurs when usage telemetry is disabled. The eventual telemetry log call becomes a no-op, but the expensive collection has already happened.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the standalone Agents/Sessions window with no normal workspace folder open.
2. Create a new agent session whose effective working directory is a large directory such as `$HOME`.
3. Send any short foreground message.
4. Observe the renderer memory while the provider is processing the request.

## Expected Behavior

- The response renders normally.
- Telemetry-only data collection does not run when usage telemetry is disabled.
- A file count never requires materializing every matching URI in the renderer.

## Actual Behavior

- `SessionsTelemetryContribution.onWillSendRequest` starts `_startWorkspaceFileCountFetch(...)` before the provider request completes.
- `_computeWorkspaceFileCount(...)` calls `fileSearch` with `filePattern: ''` and no `maxResults`.
- The extension host runs an `rg --files` search over the session workspace and sends all matches to the renderer.
- `RemoteSearchProvider` stores every revived URI in `SearchOperation.matches`, then converts the complete map to an array even though the caller only needs `results.length`.
- In this reproduction, renderer heap use increased from approximately 76 MiB to 3.56 GiB in about 18 seconds. DOM nodes and event-listener counts remained roughly flat.
- The provider completed and persisted its final response before the renderer crashed. Reloading the window could then reveal the already-completed response, which explains an associated “first response is blank, reload shows it” symptom.
- The macOS crash report recorded `Code Helper (Renderer)`, `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP`, termination code 5. Allocation sampling was dominated by extension-host search-result RPC deserialization and URI revival.

Sanitized memory samples from the renderer:

| Time relative to send | Heap used | JS heap used | DOM nodes | JS listeners |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| before send | 76.4 MiB | 76.4 MiB | 4,103 | 5,618 |
| +11 s | 1,007.1 MiB | 903.9 MiB | 2,870 | 2,834 |
| +20 s | 3,166.3 MiB | 2,950.8 MiB | 2,717 | 2,834 |
| +23 s | 3,557.2 MiB | 3,217.6 MiB | 2,694 | 2,893 |

The dominant allocation stack was:

```text
deserializeRequestJSONArgs
→ $handleFileMatch
→ handleFindMatch / addMatch
→ URI.revive / URI.toJSON
```

## Relevant Source

The behavior is present in both the installed 1.128.1 source and current `main` as of this report:

- The foreground send hook starts the count unconditional

title: `workspaceContains` glob activation events are silently defeated by default `files.exclude` (`**/.git`, `**/.svn`, `**/.hg`), so extensions cannot activate on descendant SCM metadata
body:
- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (commit `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7`)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled: N/A (behavior of extension activation itself; reproduced with a minimal probe extension in an isolated `--user-data-dir`/`--extensions-dir`, default settings)

### Summary

Any `workspaceContains` activation event containing `*` or `?` is routed through file search, and that search applies the configured excludes — including the *default* `files.exclude` entries `**/.git`, `**/.svn`, `**/.hg`. As a result, a glob activation event that targets SCM metadata (for example `workspaceContains:**/.svn/wc.db` for a Subversion extension) can never fire, even when the file demonstrably exists in the workspace. Exact (glob-free) patterns use a separate `exists()` branch and are unaffected — but exact patterns cannot express "a working copy in some child directory whose name I don't know".

The practical consequence: an SCM extension for Subversion/Mercurial (or anything keyed off dot-directory metadata) has no `workspaceContains` form that activates when the working copy is a *descendant* of the opened folder. The only workarounds are `onStartupFinished`/`*` (activating in every workspace, which `workspaceContains` exists to avoid) or asking the user to open the working-copy root.

This is silent: nothing in the extension host log indicates the pattern was suppressed by an exclude; the extension simply never activates.

### Minimal repro

Probe extension (plain JS, no build step) — one activation event per extension so the fired event is unambiguous; on activation it writes a marker file:

```json
{
  "name": "svnprobe-glob-file",
  "publisher": "svnprobe",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "engines": { "vscode": "^1.85.0" },
  "main": "./extension.js",
  "activationEvents": ["workspaceContains:**/.svn/wc.db"],
  "capabilities": { "untrustedWorkspaces": { "supported": true } }
}
```

Fixtures (file contents irrelevant; existence matters):

```
wc-root/            .svn/wc.db          # working copy at workspace root
parent-ws/          child/.svn/wc.db    # working copy in a child dir (the real-world case)
no-svn/             plain.txt           # negative control
```

Steps:
1. Install probes into an isolated instance: `code --user-data-dir <ud> --extensions-dir <ext> --install-extension <vsix>`.
2. Open each fixture folder; wait past the workspaceContains window; check markers.

### Observed (3 identical runs, isolated instance, default settings)

| activation event | wc-root (`.svn/wc.db` at root) | parent-ws (`child/.svn/wc.db`) | no-svn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspaceContains:.svn/wc.db` (exact) | activates | no (correct: path not at root) | no |
| `workspaceContains:**/.svn/wc.db` | **no** | **no** | no |
| `workspaceContains:**/.svn` | no | no | no |
| `workspaceContains:*/.svn` | no | no | no |
| `workspaceContains:*/*/.svn` | no | no | no |

Note the wc-root row: the exact pattern and the `**/` glob describe the *same existing file*, in the same launch, and only the exact one fires.

Public-API confirmation from inside the activated probe (same workspace, `child/.svn/wc.db` present):

```js
await vscode.workspace.findFiles('**/.svn/wc.db', undefined, 10) // [] — default excludes applied
await vscode.workspace.findFiles('**/.svn/wc.db', null, 10)      // [ '<ws>/.svn/wc.db', '<ws>/child/.svn/wc.db' ]
```

body: Type: Bug On macOS 26 (Tahoe), VS Code windows are repeatedly killed with _"The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'killed', code: '9')"_. This is not a crash and not an OOM kill: the kernel terminates `Code Helper (Renderer)` with a **fatal EXC_RESOURCE exception for Mach port-space exhaustion** (~267,000 ports, the per-task cap). 11 windows were killed this way over 5 days across unrelated workspaces. title: Bug / UX Flaw: workbench.action.openAgentsWindow breaks default text editing binding (Toggle Block Comment)
body:
Type: Bug ### Summary The keybinding `Ctrl+Shift+A` assigned to `workbench.action.openAgentsWindow` conflicts directly with core text-editing functionality and user expectations. Furthermore, its `when` context clause is overly broad, capturing keystrokes even while `editorTextFocus` is active. ### Problem Description 1. **Context Overlap:** When editing code, pressing `Ctrl+Shift+A` invokes `workbench.action.openAgentsWindow` instead of block commenting or user-customized editor actions, because the new Agent/Chat conditions take precedence over editor scope. 2. **Keybinding Space Exhaustion:** Finding an unassigned `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `[Letter]` shortcut is mathematically and practically constrained due to: - Operating System reserved global shortcuts (Windows/Linux/macOS). - International keyboard layout incompatibilities with non-alphanumeric keys. - High density of existing default shortcuts in VS Code. Because of this, assigning a single-stage primary shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+A`) to a secondary feature like the Agents Window inevitably breaks core workflows for developers. ### Probabilistic & Combinatorial Issue Assuming standard 26-letter layouts: - A large percentage of direct `Ctrl+Shift+[A-Z]` combinations are already mapped by either the host OS, accessibility features, or core editor actions. - Assigning new AI/Chat features to primary single-stage hotkeys creates a high-probability collision risk for non-English layouts or existing user bindings. ### Suggested Solution - **Option A (Recommended):** Change `workbench.action.openAgentsWindow` to a chord shortcut (e.g., `Ctrl+K Ctrl+A` or `Ctrl+Cmd+A`), which is the established standard in VS Code for secondary or feature-specific panels. - **Option B:** Restrict the `when` clause of `workbench.action.openAgentsWindow` so it explicitly yields when `editorTextFocus` is `true`. ### Environment - **VS Code Version:** [Tu versión actual de VS Code] - **OS:** [Tu sistema operativo, e.g., Windows 11 / Linux / macOS] VS Code version: Code 1.129.1 (8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8, 2026-07-17T15:35:09Z) OS version: Linux x64 7.0.0-28-generic snap Modes:

title: MCP model access permissions fail silently, making working servers appear broken
body:
Describe the feature you’d like

When an MCP server requires model access (for example, to perform sampling), VS Code should explicitly notify the user if the currently selected model has not been granted permission to be used by that MCP server.

Currently, this failure is difficult to discover. From the user’s perspective, the MCP server appears to be malfunctioning, even though the actual issue is simply a missing model access permission.

This is especially confusing because:

* The MCP server starts successfully.
* The server is visible in VS Code.
* Tools may even be listed correctly.
* There is no obvious indication that the selected model is not allowed to access the server.

As a result, many users naturally assume that:

* the MCP server is broken,
* OAuth or authentication is misconfigured,
* or the MCP implementation itself has a bug.

Only users who already know about Configure Model Access are likely to identify the real cause.

Expected behavior

Instead of failing silently, VS Code should provide a clear and actionable message such as:

This MCP server is not permitted to use the selected model.

Actions could include:

* Grant Access
* Configure Model Access

or automatically open the model access configuration dialog.

Why this would help

The current security model makes sense—requiring explicit permission before an MCP server can use a model is a reasonable default.

The issue is discoverability, not security.

A clear permission prompt or error message would significantly improve the onboarding and debugging experience while preserving the existing security model.

Instead of spending time debugging a perfectly healthy MCP server, users would immediately understand that the missing permission is the only issue.

title: Chat custom endpoint: API key stored with trailing newline, causing 403 on all requests
body:
## Summary

When configuring a custom LLM endpoint in VS Code, the API key is stored in SecretStorage with a trailing `\n`, causing every request to fail with a 403.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy an API key from a terminal — e.g. `op item get my-api-key --field credential --reveal | pbcopy`. The clipboard includes a trailing newline (standard shell behaviour).
2. Open VS Code and configure a custom endpoint via the Chat model picker or `chatLanguageModels.json`.
3. Paste the key into the input dialog and press Enter to confirm.
4. VS Code stores `key\n` instead of `key` in SecretStorage (`chat.lm.secret.*`).
5. Every request to the custom endpoint fails: `403 token expired or invalid`.

## Expected behaviour

VS Code should trim whitespace (at minimum `\n` / `\r\n`) from the API key value before calling `context.secrets.store()`.

## Why this is not user error

Pressing Enter is the **only** way to confirm the input dialog — users cannot avoid it. Trailing newlines in clipboard content are ubiquitous (shell commands, password managers, terminal copies all append `\n`). The fix is a single `.trim()` call on the stored value; the burden should not be on the user to strip the newline before pasting.

## Workaround

Strip the newline before copying to clipboard:
```bash
op item get my-api-key --field credential --reveal | tr -d '\n' | pbcopy
```

## Environment

- VS Code 1.130.0 (darwin arm64)
- Custom endpoint via `chatLanguageModels.json` with `${input:chat.lm.secret.*}` reference
- Confirmed by inspecting `state.vscdb` — the decrypted secret contains a trailing `0x0A` byte

## Suggested fix

In the custom endpoint configuration flow, before storing the secret:
```ts
await context.secrets.store(secretKey, apiKey.trim());
```

title: API: Provide a stable terminal session ID across window reloads
body:
Extensions can observe terminals through `vscode.window.terminals` and `vscode.window.onDidOpenTerminal`, but there is no public stable identity that allows an extension to correlate the same logical terminal session before and after `Developer: Reload Window`.

After a reload, VS Code may successfully reattach the existing persistent terminal process, but the extension host receives a new `Terminal` object. None of the currently public properties can be used as identity:

- `Terminal.processId` identifies a process, not a logical terminal session. It may remain the same after a window reload, but it can change when VS Code revives a persistent session by creating a new process.
- `Terminal.name` and the terminal tab title are mutable and can change to the foreground process name.
- `cwd` is neither unique nor guaranteed to be available through `Terminal.creationOptions`.
- Multiple terminals may intentionally have identical creation options.
- Extension-provided values in `TerminalOptions.env` are not reliably available in `Terminal.creationOptions` after persistent reattach.

This prevents an extension that manages multiple long-lived terminals from restoring its own state without guessing based on process IDs, titles, working directories, or process environment inspection.

## Proposed API contract

Please expose an opaque terminal session ID on `Terminal`, for example:

```ts
interface Terminal {
    /**
     * An opaque identifier for this logical terminal session.
     *
     * The value remains stable when the terminal is restored or reattached
     * across window and extension-host reloads.
     */
    readonly sessionId: string;
}
```

The exact property name is not important. The required behavior is:

1. Every newly created logical terminal session receives a unique ID.
2. The ID is available on the `Terminal` returned by `createTerminal`, in `window.terminals`, and in `onDidOpenTerminal`.
3. The ID remains unchanged across `Developer: Reload Window` when VS Code restores or reattaches that terminal.
4. The ID also represents the same logical session if persistent-session revival recreates the underlying process and therefore changes `processId`.
5. Once a terminal session is disposed, a subsequently created terminal gets a different ID.
6. The value is opaque. It does not need to expose a PTY ID, process metadata, environment variables, or other internal reconnection data.

## Example use case

An extension creates several terminal editors for long-running development environments and stores per-terminal state:

```ts
const terminal = vscode.window.createTerminal({
    name: 'Managed terminal',
    location: {
        viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.Active,
        preserveFocus: true
    }
});

await extensionContext.globalState.update(
    `terminal.${terminal.sessionId}`,
    persistedExtensionState
);
```

After a window reload, the extension should be able to enumerate `window.terminals`, read the same `sessionId`, and reconnect its state to the already restored terminal without launching a replacement process.

## Why an opaque ID is preferable

This capability does not require exposing the terminal's resolved process environment or internal reconnection metadata. It gives extensions identity without encouraging process inspection or overloading mutable presentation fields such as the terminal name.

## Related issues

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237127 reports that `Terminal.creationOptions.shellPath`

title: Chat plugins: auto-discover worktree-root plugin.json in trusted worktree windows
body:
## Problem

I'm developing a VS Code agent plugin in a Git worktree, but VS Code doesn't appear to load the plugin from the active worktree. Instead it seems to resolve another copy/version of the plugin. 

What is a work-tree-specific setup that allows VSCode to resolve plugin.json in the scope of each git work-tree directory? 

## Worktree scenario

```text
repo.worktrees/
  main/plugin.json
  feature-a/plugin.json    # branch-specific copy
  feature-b/plugin.json    # branch-specific copy
```

1. Create or detect multiple Git worktrees.
2. Run **Git: Open Worktree in New Window** and select `feature-a`.
3. The trusted worktree root contains `plugin.json`.
4. There is no worktree-local opt-in without a global user setting or absolute path.
5. Open `feature-b`; the desired source is now that worktree's root copy.

## Expected behavior

Support a worktree-local plugin source for trusted workspaces. For example:

- Detect `plugin.json` at each trusted workspace-folder root.
- Prompt once to enable it, or expose a workspace-local enablement toggle.
- Resolve components relative to that worktree root.
- Keep enablement isolated per workspace/worktree.
- Do not recursively load sibling worktrees or the parent worktree container.

## Related work

- #303853 requests workspace-scoped `chat.pluginLocations`.
- #315123 is an open PR changing it to `ConfigurationScope.WINDOW`.
- #308791 requests recursive discovery under a common parent.

This request is specifically worktree-root discovery/enablement. If #315123 is the intended solution, this scenario would be useful validation coverage and documentation.

## Screenshot

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders `1.131.0-insider`
- Commit `29215ba85809234979befc6b0d1fb4b0ab884383`
- Windows x64

## Current workaround

```jsonc
"chat.pluginLocations": {
  ".": true
}
```

This resolves per window, but globally opts every workspace into root plugin discovery rather than providing worktree-local enablement.

title: Workspace skill descriptions can alter customization-index structure and suppress external-file confirmation
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: `0.59.0`
- VS Code Version: latest `main`, commit `dd862885ff5fbd279747c793e18105e6b7ddc805`
- OS Version: Windows 11 `10.0.26200` build `26200`
- Feature: Agent mode, workspace skills, ReadFile tool
- Selected model: No live model is required for the deterministic test
- Logs: Local unit-test output only; no production service was contacted

## Summary

A workspace skill description is inserted into the XML-like chat customizations index without structural escaping. The generated text is later parsed back into instruction and skill file sets used by the external-file ReadFile confirmation logic.

As a result, delimiter characters in workspace-controlled skill metadata can alter the generated index structure and cause an outside-workspace URI to be classified as an instruction file. ReadFile then omits the confirmation that the safe control receives.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out commit `dd862885ff5fbd279747c793e18105e6b7ddc805`.
2. Create a workspace `SKILL.md` whose valid frontmatter description contains XML delimiter characters that terminate the generated description element and introduce a synthetic instruction/file record.
3. Build the customizations index through `AutomaticInstructionsCollector`.
4. Parse the generated index through `CustomInstructionsService.parseInstructionIndexFile`.
5. Prepare a ReadFile invocation for the synthetic outside-workspace URI.
6. Compare it with an otherwise identical control using a normal skill description.

Local deterministic test result on latest `main`:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

The control produced confirmation messages. The structurally altered index did not.

## Expected Behavior

Workspace-controlled skill names, descriptions, and paths should be encoded as data and must not be able to add records to the generated customization index or influence external-file authorization.

## Actual Behavior

The skill description is interpolated as markup. The later index parser accepts the additional structure, and the resulting URI is treated as an external instruction file for which ReadFile confirmation is not shown.

## Relevant Source

- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/promptFiles/node/automaticInstructionsCollector.ts:497-504` constructs the skill entry and interpolates `skill.description`.
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/customInstructions/common/customInstructionsService.ts:501-585` parses the model-facing text back into instruction and skill URI sets.
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/toolUtils.ts:217-233` exempts URIs present in those parsed sets from the normal outside-workspace rejection.
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/readFileTool.tsx:207-244` prepares the ReadFile confirmation.

## Impact and Scope

This is a confirmation/security-boundary consistency issue. It can cause a file outside the workspace to be returned to the configured model without the expected external-file confirmation.

The reproduced behavior requires the outer Copilot/workspace-trust requirements and an agent ReadFile request for the affected path. The test does not demonstrate command execution or direct exfiltration to a workspace-controlled server.

## Suggested Fix

- Escape every dynamic field before including it in the model-facing XML-like representation.
- Prefer a structured, non-text authorization object rather than reparsing prompt text.
- Do not derive external-file authorization from a represen

title: [semantic] Add a `parameter` semantic token modifier
body:
I am working on a theme that styles parameters in italics and functions in pink.

For a regular parameter, this works as expected:

```ts
function f(a: string) {
  console.log(a);
}
```

The semantic token classifications are `parameter.declaration` at declaration, and `parameter` at usage.

The issue appears with a function-valued parameter:

```ts
function f(a: string, cb: () => string) {
  cb();
}
```

In this case, `cb` is classified as `function.declaration` at declaration, and `function` at usage.

That classification is understandable because `cb` denotes a callable value. However, `cb` is also a parameter accepted by `f`. It is therefore incomplete for theming purposes because the parameter role is lost. Semantic tokens require the provider to choose one standard token type, so themes cannot express both styling intentions.

I would like `cb` to receive parameter styling (italic) and function styling (pink), but there is no selector that can apply italics specifically to function-valued parameters without also affecting unrelated function declarations or usages.

Proposed solution: add a standard `parameter` semantic token modifier.

Existing classifications remain unchanged while gaining the modifier:

Regular parameter declaration: `parameter.declaration.parameter`

Regular parameter usage: `parameter.parameter`

Function-valued parameter declaration: `function.declaration.parameter`

Function-valued parameter usage: `function.parameter`

This would allow themes to style every parameter using:

```json
"*.parameter": {
  "fontStyle": "italic"
}
```

Function-valued parameters would still match existing `function` rules and receive their function color:

```json
"function": {
  "foreground": "#ff69b4"
}
```

For tokens whose standard type is already `parameter`, the modifier can be emitted for consistency (`parameter.parameter`), or omitted as redundant. Either representation would be compatible with existing themes, although the former would require themes to style both `parameter` and `*.parameter`.

The proposal is additive:

* existing themes continue matching `parameter` and `function`
* existing providers remain valid
* providers can add the new modifier incrementally
* newer themes can use `*.parameter`
* no current primary token type needs to be renamed or reinterpreted

The desired classifications would be (with modifier `parameter` provided for standard `parameter`):

a at declaration: `parameter.declaration.parameter`

a at usage: `parameter.parameter`

cb at declaration: `function.declaration.parameter`

cb at usage: `function.parameter`

`parameter` becomes usable as an orthogonal fact: "This symbol is accepted as an input by the surrounding declaration.". That applies regardless of whether the standard type is `parameter`, `function`, or another future token type.

The open questions are
- whether `parameter` is suitable as a standard modifier,
- whether it should apply to standard `parameter` as well.
- whether `typeParameter` should also recieve the `parameter` modifier, or the feature should remain intended for runtime parameter constructs.

title: Agent Host: Copilot steering messages drop their attachments, so the agent never sees them
body:
### Description

In the Agents window, an attachment (image, file, selection) added to a message that is sent **while a Copilot agent is already busy** is silently dropped and never reaches the model. The message text arrives, the attachment chip renders in the UI, and nothing is logged as an error -- the agent simply behaves as if no attachment was provided (e.g. "I don't see an image").

This only affects the **steering** path (send while the agent is mid-turn) on the **Copilot** provider. It looks intermittent to users because whether an attachment survives depends purely on whether the agent happened to be busy at the moment they pressed send.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start a **Copilot** agent session.
2. Send a prompt that takes a while (so the agent is mid-turn).
3. **While it is still running**, attach an image and send a message such as "what is in this image?".
4. The message is delivered as a steering message and the agent responds to the text.

**Expected:** the agent receives the attachment and can describe the image.
**Actual:** the attachment is not in the model payload; the agent says it received no image.

Sending the exact same message when the agent is **idle** works correctly.

### Root Cause

`CopilotAgentSession.sendSteering` forwards only the text and never passes the attachments to the SDK:

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`

```ts
async sendSteering(steeringMessage: PendingMessage): Promise<void> {
    ...
    await this._wrapper.session.send({
        prompt: steeringMessage.message.text,
        mode: 'immediate',
    });
```

`steeringMessage.message.attachments` is simply not read. The normal (idle) path in the same file does it correctly -- it maps attachments via `_toSdkAttachment` and passes them to `session.send({ prompt, attachments })`.

Everything upstream of this call does its job, which is what makes the drop so quiet:

- `AgentService._rewriteUserMessageAttachments` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`) runs for `ChatPendingMessageSetAction` as well as `ChatTurnStartedAction`, so a steering message's attachments are already materialized to local files on the agent host side (`_rewriteSingleAttachment` -> `_readClientResource` -> `_writeAndRewrite`) before the provider is called.
- `PendingMessage.message` is a full `Message` and does carry `attachments` at this point.
- `CopilotAgent.setPendingMessages` routes only the steering message through `sendSteering`; **queued** messages are dispatched by the server through the normal `sendMessage` path, so queued messages keep their attachments and steering messages do not.

The other providers already handle this correctly, which confirms Copilot is the outlier:

- Claude -- `ClaudeAgentSession.injectSteering` (`node/claude/claudeAgentSession.ts`) passes `steeringMessage.message.attachments` to `resolvePromptToContentBlocks`.
- Codex -- `codexAgent.ts` calls `resolveCodexInput(text, steeringMessage.message.attachments)`.

### Proposed Fix

Mirror the normal send path in `sendSteering`: map `steeringMessage.message.attachments` through `_toSdkAttachment` and pass the result as `attachments` alongside `mode: 'immediate'`. This is a Copilot-only change of roughly five lines, plus a regression test in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` asserting that a steering message with attachments reaches `session.send` with those attachments.

### Notes

Found by code inspection while investigating attac

title: Feature Request: Smart file name suggestion for untitled files by detecting specific extensions in top comments
body:
### Feature Description

Currently, when saving an untitled file (e.g., Untitled-1), VS Code reads the very first line of text to suggest a file name in the "Save As" dialog. While helpful, it has two limitations when users write the intended file name in a comment at the top:

1. It only checks the literal first line. If there is a blank line or a different comment before it, the feature fails.
2. It includes comment characters (like `# ` in Python) in the suggested name, forcing the user to manually backspace and delete them every time.

### Proposed Solution

I would like to suggest a smarter detection mechanism for untitled files:

1. **Scan the first few lines:** Instead of looking only at line 1, look through the first 5–10 lines for any line containing a valid file extension (like `.py`, `.js`, etc.).
2. **Clean comment characters:** If a line like `# my_program.py` or `// script.js` is detected, automatically strip the comment symbols, slashes, and leading/trailing whitespaces before injecting it into the "Save As" field.

This would drastically speed up the workflow for developers who prefer to draft quick code and quickly save it without using heavy AI extensions or leaving the keyboard. Thank you!

title: Agent Host terminal auto-approve should use PowerShell grammar for PowerShell commands
body:
Follow up to #326766 and #324136. PR #327947 adds persistent user/workspace auto-approve actions to Agent Host Copilot terminal confirmations, but there is still a parser mismatch for the SDK's `powershell` tool.

The workbench generates suggestions using the PowerShell tree-sitter grammar, while Agent Host's `commandAutoApprover.ts` only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` for eligibility and enforcement.

Impact:

- **Existing settings rule:** a simple rule such as `"Get-ChildItem": true` usually works because bash can treat it as a generic command name. Rules for PowerShell-specific syntax can still miss because Agent Host splits/interprets the command using bash grammar.
- **Rule added from #327947:** the workbench can suggest and persist a rule from an accurate PowerShell parse, but Agent Host re-parses the next command as bash. The user selects "Always Allow" and is prompted again.
- **Exact command-line rule:** this can also miss when bash parsing fails because Agent Host parses before checking the exact command-line allow rule.

Representative cases include pipelines with script blocks (`Where-Object { ... }`), `$()` subexpressions, backtick continuations, PowerShell operators, and PowerShell-specific redirects such as `$null`.

The expected failure mode is conservative re-prompting/inconsistent suggestions; Agent Host remains authoritative for approval. There is no known auto-approval bypass from this mismatch.

Work needed:

- Load `tree-sitter-powershell.wasm` in the Agent Host command auto-approver (it already ships in the same package).
- Carry/select the shell grammar for both rule eligibility and enforcement.
- Add coverage for existing settings rules and rules created from #327947, including PowerShell-specific sub-command and exact-command-line cases.

Related forwarding work: #322774.

Agent Host session read/unread state is not synced between the editor window and the agents window
body:
Read/unread state for an Agent Host session is tracked separately by each surface, so the two windows disagree about whether a session has been read.

- The **agents window** already routes read state through the Agent Host: `ISession.isRead` is backed by the protocol `IsRead` status bit, which the host persists and fans out to connected clients.
- The **editor window** does not. `AgentSessionsModel` keeps its own read *timestamps* in `IStorageService`, with no path to or from the host.

The result: opening a session in one window leaves it showing as unread in the other, and a session the host marks unread after background output doesn't surface as unread in the editor window.

There is a second, related problem inside the host itself. Read state has two parallel representations — the `SessionStatus.IsRead` bit and standalone `isRead` / `isArchived` booleans on the local `IAgentSessionMetadata` IPC shape. Different code paths read different ones, and `listSessions()` could return the two disagreeing. Any fix needs one source of truth rather than a third consumer of an ambiguous pair.

This is host-owned rather than agent-owned, so it applies equally to Copilot, Claude, and Codex sessions — none of those SDKs track read state themselves.

## How to verify

1. Open a workspace and start an Agent Host session (Copilot, Claude, or Codex) from the agents window. Send a prompt and let the turn finish.
2. Leave the session **unread**: navigate away in the agents window without opening it after the turn completes. It should show an unread indicator.
3. Open the **editor window** (Chat Sessions view) for the same workspace and find that session in the list.
   - **Expected:** it shows as unread in both windows.
   - **Before the fix:** the two windows disagree.
4. Click the session in the editor window to open it, then switch back to the agents window.
   - **Expected:** it is now marked read in the agents window too, without a reload.
5. Do the reverse: right-click the session in the agents window → **Mark as Unread**, then check the editor window's list.
   - **Expected:** it shows as unread there as well.
6. With the session sitting idle and read, send it a message from one window and let the turn complete while the session is not being viewed.
   - **Expected:** both windows show it as unread once the turn finishes.

Reloading either window should preserve whatever the host last recorded, since the state is persisted host-side rather than in per-window storage.

Fixed by #327950.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Agent Host: stream rich tool call progress while the model generates arguments
body:
## Problem

In Agent Host sessions, a tool call stays a bare "running" row until the model has finished generating its entire argument payload. For a large `apply_patch` or file create/edit, that can be many seconds where the UI says nothing about what the agent is doing.

The old extension-host VS Code agent did better: it consumed streaming argument deltas and fed them to per-tool `handleToolStream` formatters, so the row showed the file being edited and a line count that ticked up while the patch was still being generated. Agent Host lost that behavior.

## Expected

While the model is generating tool arguments, the tool row should progressively show what the call is going to do — the target file as a clickable widget, and a line count that updates as the payload grows. For example:

- `Creating result.txt (12 lines)`
- `Replacing 2 lines with 3 lines in file.ts`
- `Generating patch (48 lines) in file.ts`

This should work for the built-in edit-shaped tools across providers, and degrade gracefully for tools that have no rich formatter.

## Notes

- Both bundled SDKs already expose the needed events: Copilot `assistant.tool_call_delta` and Claude `input_json_delta`. Codex reports complete tool items at `item/started`, so it has no equivalent argument-generation stream today.
- AHP already has the Start → Delta → Ready tool-call lifecycle, so this does not require a new action; the progress can ride on the existing Delta.
- Growing edit bodies should not need to cross the wire just to render a row — the host can compute the display message and send that instead.

## Related

- #321196 — same symptom on the extension-host BYOK / Responses API path (`model-byok`). Different code path, tracked separately.

(Written by Copilot)

title: BYOK models in AgentHost sessions do not expose reasoning effort (thinking level) configuration
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.131.0
- OS Version: macOS

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure a BYOK model that supports reasoning effort (e.g. Anthropic Claude or OpenAI o-series) via the Copilot extension's BYOK settings
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` in settings and restart the Agent Host process
3. Open an AgentHost Copilot session, open the model picker, and select the BYOK model
4. Observe: the thinking effort / reasoning effort configuration option is missing

**Expected:** The BYOK model in the AgentHost picker should expose the same reasoning effort configuration (e.g. Low / Medium / High) that is available in the regular Copilot Chat model picker.

**Actual:** The BYOK model shows in the picker but has no thinking effort selector. The same model shows the reasoning effort option correctly in the regular (non-AgentHost) Copilot Chat model picker.

## Root Cause

The BYOK bridge DTO (`IByokLmModelInfo`) between the renderer and the Agent Host process has never carried reasoning effort information. This is a gap in the bridge design, not a regression — the `configSchema` was simply never included when the model metadata DTO was incrementally built up.

**Data flow comparison:**

| Path | `configSchema` | Reasoning Effort |
|------|---------------|-----------------|
| CAPI models → `_listModels()` | ✅ `_createModelConfigSchema()` synthesizes `thinkingLevel` | ✅ |
| BYOK models → `_refreshByokModels()` | ❌ not set | ❌ |

The renderer-side `AgentHostByokLmHandler.listModels()` has access to `metadata.configurationSchema` (which includes `reasoningEffort` set by the Copilot extension's `byokModelInfo.ts`) but does not read or forward it. Consequently, `CopilotAgent._refreshByokModels()` cannot synthesize a `configSchema` for BYOK models, and `AgentHostLanguageModelProvider` receives `configSchema: undefined`.

## Proposed Fix

Three surgical changes thread reasoning effort through the bridge:

**1. `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostByokLm.ts`** — add fields to `IByokLmModelInfo`:
```typescript
readonly supportsReasoningEffort?: readonly string[];

title: Wrong link color in plan widget
Agent Host can delete durable sessions after transient resume failures
body:
## Problem

An existing Agent Host session can disappear permanently after a transient Copilot SDK resume failure.

The SDK reports both genuinely empty sessions and unrelated failures with JSON-RPC code `-32603`. Agent Host treated nearly every `-32603` as an empty session and replaced the existing SDK session with a new empty session using the same ID.

When that zero-turn state later lost its final subscriber, empty-session GC treated it as an abandoned provisional draft and invoked destructive disposal. That deleted the SDK event history, Agent Host session database, and worktree.

## Expected

- Network, authentication, corruption, and unknown resume failures preserve all durable session data and surface the error.
- Empty-session recreation is limited to explicit SDK `no events` and `Session not found` responses.
- Destructive empty-session GC only applies to pristine provisional sessions that have never materialized or persisted data.
- Chat, changeset, and annotations subscriptions keep their owning session alive.

## Additional context

The issue was reproduced with session `f72992a0-b278-45e0-b094-4e78dd0b1370`. Its exported debug bundle retained 2,552 SDK events, including 10 user messages, immediately before Agent Host GC deleted the live session.

Fix: [#328540](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328540)

(Written by Copilot)

title: Agent Host auto-approves sed in-place edits
body:
## Problem

Agent Host's terminal auto-approval rules allow normal `sed` commands, but do not distinguish in-place editing forms such as:

```bash
sed -i 's/foo/bar/' file.txt
sed --in-place 's/foo/bar/' file.txt
```

These forms modify files through command arguments rather than shell redirects, so the existing redirect write check does not see them. As a result, a recognized `sed` command can be auto-approved even though it edits a file directly.

Workbench already detects canonical `sed` in-place forms through its command-specific file-write parser.

## Expected

- Agent Host should require confirmation for canonical `sed` in-place forms, including `-i`, `-I`, clustered/backup-suffix variants, BSD empty suffixes, and `--in-place`.
- A configured full-command allow rule should not override this check.
- Normal non-in-place `sed` commands should retain their existing auto-approval behavior.
- Workbench file-write behavior and settings should remain unchanged.

Broader shell-dialect and dynamic-option hardening is tracked separately in #328898.
