title: Terminal auto-approval allows git show file output without confirmation
body:
## Problem

Terminal auto-approval treats `git show` as a read-only command, but `git show` can write directly to a file through its `--output` option:

```bash
git show --format=%B --output=message.txt HEAD
git show --output message.txt HEAD
```

Because `--output` is a Git option rather than a shell redirect, it does not produce a tree-sitter `file_redirect` node. The write-destination check is therefore not consulted, and the command can be auto-approved.

The existing default rules already require confirmation for `git log --output`, but not for the equivalent `git show` option.

## Expected

- `git show --output=<path>` and `git show --output <path>` require confirmation in both workbench and Agent Host terminal auto-approval.
- Plain `git show`, `git show --format=...`, and similarly named options remain auto-approved.
- Workbench and Agent Host use the same default Git rule definitions.

title: Harden PowerShell terminal auto-approval parsing and default rules
body:
PowerShell terminal auto-approval currently relies on tree-sitter command captures and broad default rules. Several cases should require the normal terminal confirmation instead of being auto-approved from an incomplete or overly broad interpretation of the command line.

This issue tracks the VS Code-owned mitigation across both workbench and Agent Host terminal auto-approval:

- Share the PowerShell parse-safety policy between workbench and Agent Host.
- Require confirmation when tree-sitter reports an incomplete PowerShell parse, even when surviving command captures match allow rules.
- Keep assignment, method invocation, scriptblock invocation, and expression-pipeline syntax outside auto-approval when the parser cannot safely reduce it to command rules.
- Replace broad `Select-*`, `Measure-*`, `Compare-*`, `Format-*`, and `Sort-*` defaults with an explicit shared list of known cmdlets.
- Tighten the POSIX `sort` default so case-insensitive PowerShell matching cannot approve arbitrary `Sort-*` cmdlets.
- Keep clean PowerShell parses, Bash behavior, and user-configured auto-approval rules unchanged.
- Add parity coverage for workbench and Agent Host, including incomplete/escaped syntax, invocation expressions, pipelines, explicit safe cmdlets, and arbitrary verb-prefixed cmdlet names.

When a command is not auto-approved, it should show the normal confirmation and remain runnable if the user allows it; this is not a hard execution block.

Related consolidation debt: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329028

title: Require confirmation for CMD delayed-expansion redirect destinations
body:
Terminal auto-approval can treat a file redirect destination containing balanced CMD delayed environment-variable expansion, such as `!VARIABLE!\file.txt`, as a literal path relative to the terminal working directory.

The final destination is resolved later by CMD when delayed expansion is enabled, so the pre-expansion text is not authoritative for workspace containment.

Expected behavior:

- Recognize balanced, non-empty CMD delayed-expansion syntax in redirect destinations.
- Require the normal terminal confirmation instead of classifying the target as workspace-local.
- Keep ordinary or unmatched `!` characters eligible for auto-approval.
- Apply the same destination-safety behavior in workbench and Agent Host terminal permission checks.
- Preserve existing Bash, PowerShell, literal-path, and file-write setting behavior.

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329055

title: Restrict terminal auto-approval settings in untrusted workspaces
body:
Terminal auto-approval safety settings are currently workspace-overridable while a workspace is untrusted. Neighboring terminal safety settings already use `restricted: true`, so untrusted workspace configuration should not be able to change these controls either.

This issue tracks the VS Code-owned mitigation:

- Mark terminal auto-approval enablement, command rules, default-rule overrides, and detected file-write policy as restricted settings.
- Also restrict the deprecated `chat.agent.terminal.autoApprove` compatibility setting.
- Ignore workspace-provided values for these settings while the workspace is untrusted.
- Preserve user, remote, default, and trusted-workspace behavior.
- Keep terminal, Agent Host, warning, sandbox, and permission logic unchanged.
- Add parser-level regressions for untrusted single-folder and `.code-workspace` settings, plus a trusted-workspace negative control.

Affected settings:

- `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove`
- `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove`
- `chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules`
- `chat.tools.terminal.blockDetectedFileWrites`
- `chat.agent.terminal.autoApprove` (deprecated compatibility path)

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329069

Related consolidation debt: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329028

- OS Version: (unspecified)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code (build from main or an Insider that includes commit f9c1c7e32ab9 / the revert) or use a binary where floating panels are enabled.
2. Arrange the workbench so floating panels and sidebars are present (e.g., panel-position-bottom, sidebars visible) so sashes sit between floating cards.
3. Hover over the sash or a floating panel/title area to reveal hoverable UI (tabs/tooltips/controls), then move the pointer away.

Expected behavior:
- Hovered UI (tabs/menus) closes when the pointer leaves the hover area.

Actual behavior:
- Hovered tabs/controls remain open ("sticky") and do not close when the pointer leaves. This appears related to recent changes to floating panel margins / sash geometry; see the revert commit linked below.

Additional information / context:
- The issue appears connected to the commit that reverted "Reduce floating panel margins for layout consistency" (revert commit f9c1c7e32ab929855d93badc42b31226fec4e44e).
- File of interest: src/vs/workbench/browser/media/floatingPanels.css (changes to trailing margins and sash transforms affect hit region/hover geometry).
- Commit permalink: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f9c1c7e32ab929855d93badc42b31226fec4e44e
- Related comment/reference: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f9c1c7e32ab929855d93badc42b31226fec4e44e#r195038444

Notes for maintainers / proposed next steps:
- The original change reduced the trailing inter-card margin to 2px and adjusted sash width/transform math; the revert reinstates the previous margins. Reapplying the reduced margins without adjusting the sash hit/transform may cause hover hit-region asymmetry and sticky hovers.
- A suggested fix is to ensure the sash hit region and its :before highlight are re-centered on the visible gap midpoint after margin changes (adjust transform calc and inset values so the hover area covers both edges symmetrically).
- If helpful I can provide a small CSS patch proposal that keeps a 2px inter-card gap while ensuring the sash transform/size math recenters correctly and prevents sticky hovers.

Please triage and let me know if additional repro info (OS/version, screenshot/video, or a reduced test case) is needed. ok

title: Toolbar commands immediately close newly opened quick picks
body:
### Type of Bug

Regression

### Reproduction

1. Run a current VS Code Insiders build with the modern UI/style override and motion enabled.
2. Open Source Control.
3. Open a toolbar **More Actions...** menu for a repository.
4. Open **Branch** and invoke **Create Branch From...**.
5. Observe the quick pick.

This also reproduces with other commands invoked from workbench toolbars that open a quick pick. Invoking the same commands from the Command Center does not reproduce the problem.

### Expected Behavior

The command's quick pick remains open and focused.

### Actual Behavior

The Command Center/quick-pick surface briefly opens, then immediately closes and focus returns to the toolbar menu.

### Regression Details

The regression was introduced by c5f02db50896ef310d3c909628e651675644fcef ("Add open/close motion to button menus in workbench chrome", #325190).

Animated context views delay disposal for the close animation. During that interval, the closing toolbar menu remains focusable. Its existing mouse-out handling can focus the menu's `actions-container` after the command has opened and focused a quick pick. The quick pick then receives a blur event and closes.

The issue only appears when the context-view close animation is active, which explains why it reproduces on machines enrolled in the modern UI/style override but not necessarily on every machine running the same Insiders version.

### VS Code Version

Current VS Code Insiders (1.133 development cycle); regression is also present on the 1.132 release branch.

Shorten the **Create Pull Request** action label in the Agents Window to **Create PR**.

Update the user-visible action title consistently across the Agents Window, including menus, buttons, command labels, accessibility labels, and tests where applicable, without changing the underlying command ID or behavior.

title: Support editors that cannot be closed through standard user actions
body:
Add a core editor capability that allows an editor input to opt out of being closed through standard user actions across all VS Code editor groups.

When an editor has this capability, normal close affordances and commands should not close it, including:
- Tab close buttons and middle-click
- Close Editor / Close All / Close Group and related keyboard commands
- Group disposal or bulk replacement paths initiated through standard user actions

The capability should be explicit on the editor input or its capabilities, integrate with existing editor/group close flows, and expose consistent UI state (for example, no misleading enabled close affordance). Internal lifecycle operations such as shutdown, window reload, workspace transitions, or force-disposal must remain possible where required.

Add focused tests covering individual close, bulk close, group operations, and an internal forced-close/lifecycle path.

title: Agents Window: Add a Show Editor Area action
body:
Add a **Show Editor Area** action corresponding to the existing **Hide Editor Area** action in the Agents Window.

The two actions should be contextually available based on the editor-area visibility state, use consistent command/menu placement and labels, and support restoring the editor area after it has been hidden. Preserve focus behavior, layout state, accessibility, keybinding discoverability, and existing behavior outside the Agents Window.

title: Agent Host: Add server-side tools for renaming sessions and chats
body:
Add Agent Host server-side tools for renaming an agent session and an individual chat.

Agents should use these tools after creating a new session or chat to replace provisional/generated labels with a concise, meaningful name based on the work being performed.

Requirements:
- Separate, clearly scoped rename-session and rename-chat semantics (or one typed tool with equivalent clarity).
- Server-side validation, authorization, persistence, synchronization, and error reporting.
- Updated names propagate promptly to the Agents Window and other clients without requiring reload.
- Preserve user-authored names unless the rename is explicitly requested; avoid repeated automatic renaming.
- Tool descriptions should guide agents to name newly created sessions/chats at the appropriate point.

Use the GitHub Copilot app implementation in the local `github-app` checkout as design/reference material, while adapting it to Agent Host and VS Code architecture.

title: Agent Host Copilot harness treats denied client tool options as approved
body:
## Issue

In the **Agent Host Copilot harness** (not the Local harness), browser-tool confirmation choices are not honored correctly.

## Repro: Skip

1. Close all open Integrated Browser tabs.
2. Start a Copilot session using the **Agent Host Copilot harness**, not the Local harness.
3. Ask Copilot: `Please open Wikipedia.`
4. When asked for permission to open the page, choose **Skip**.

**Actual:** Copilot proceeds with the browser action even though **Skip** was selected.

**Expected:** The browser action is cancelled and no page is opened.

## Repro: Allow in Session

1. Close all open Integrated Browser tabs.
2. Start a Copilot session using the **Agent Host Copilot harness**, not the Local harness.
3. Ask Copilot: `Please open Wikipedia.`
4. When asked for permission to open the page, choose **Allow in Session**.
5. Close the Wikipedia tab that just opened
6. In the same session, ask Copilot: `Please open Bing.`
**Actual:** Copilot asks for permission again.

**Expected:** Copilot remembers the permission for the session and opens the page without prompting again.

title: Agent Host: capture git baseline checkpoint for Claude and Codex sessions (like Copilot)
body:
### Problem

Per-turn change lists for **Claude** and **Codex** sessions miss **terminal-tool edits**, but Copilot sessions show them.

The Agent Host computes per-turn changes two ways:
1. **Git checkpoint diff** — includes terminal-tool edits (needs a per-session baseline checkpoint, `turn/0`).
2. **DB `file_edits` fallback** — misses terminal-tool edits.

The git path only runs if a **baseline checkpoint** was captured. Today `captureBaselineCheckpoint` is called **only from the Copilot harness**, so Claude and Codex never capture a baseline and always fall back to the DB path.

### Fix

Do exactly what Copilot already does — **identical in every way** — for the Claude and Codex harnesses:

- Inject `IAgentHostCheckpointService` into each harness (same as Copilot).
- On the **fresh** materialize path only, call `captureBaselineCheckpoint(sessionUri, resolvedWorkingDirectories)` with the harness's resolved materialize directory set, **fire-and-forget** (`.catch`, not awaited) — identical to `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` L2511.
  - **Claude:** in `_materializeProvisional`, before the materialize event fires (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeAgent.ts` L1183).
  - **Codex:** in the first-send path after materialize, before `turn/start`, gated `!firstTurnSent && !needsResume` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts` L3569).

Copilot is unchanged. No AHP protocol changes.

### Behavior (inherited from Copilot, no new decisions)

Because the fix mirrors Copilot exactly, it inherits Copilot's existing behavior:
- **Fresh-only:** captured on first materialize, never on resume — so restored/pre-existing sessions are not backfilled.
- **Best-effort:** non-git / workspace-less sessions stay on the DB fallback.
- **Idempotent + correctly ordered:** guaranteed by the shared checkpoint service.
- **Multi-root:** unchanged — same primary-folder-only limitation Copilot has today (tracked separately).

title: agentHost: per-session provider (transport) selection for Claude sessions
body:
### Feature request

Let each **Claude** agent-host session pick a model whose **provider** decides its transport, instead of pinning the whole host to a single transport:

- `anthropic`-provider models route to the **native Anthropic SDK**.
- `copilot` (and any unknown) provider routes to the **Copilot-CAPI proxy**.

This mirrors how the Codex provider already behaves.

### Motivation

Today a Claude host is pinned to one transport, so a user can't mix a native-Anthropic model and a Copilot-routed model across sessions. Per-session provider selection removes that limitation and brings Claude in line with Codex.

### Proposed behavior

- **Provider-qualified model ids** (`@provider=anthropic:…` / `@provider=copilot:…`); bare/legacy ids resume on the host default transport (no migration needed).
- **Merged catalog** fetched from both native and proxy sources, each self-gated on its own credential/native-setup; the picker groups rows by vendor ("Anthropic" / "Copilot").
- **Per-session transport resolution** at materialize time from the selected model's provider.
- **Live switching** — selecting a model on the other transport re-materializes the session's subprocess on the next send; same-transport model changes hot-swap in place.
- **Lazy Copilot sign-in** — the Copilot resource is advertised `required: false`; sign-in defers to first send of a Copilot-routed model (matches Codex).

Addressed by #329331.

title: Agent Host Codex: allow non-Copilot sessions without GitHub Copilot sign-in
body:
Related platform capability: #318578

## Feature request

Allow the Codex Agent Host provider to run sessions using OpenAI, ChatGPT, or another configured Codex model provider without requiring GitHub Copilot sign-in.

Codex can expose both Copilot-backed and independently authenticated model providers. The selected model provider should determine the authentication required by that session; the existence of Copilot-backed models must not make GitHub sign-in a prerequisite for every Codex session or for entering the Agents window.

## Expected behavior

- Codex advertises the GitHub Copilot protected resource as optional when the agent has a usable non-GitHub model source.
- OpenAI-, ChatGPT-, local-, or custom-provider models remain available while signed out of GitHub.
- A signed-out user can create, resume, and send messages in a Codex session using one of those models.
- Copilot-backed models are advertised only when Copilot authentication is available.
- Selecting or restoring a Copilot-backed model while signed out requests GitHub Copilot authentication on demand.
- Model inventories from independently authenticated providers are additive; signing in to one provider does not implicitly change the provider used by an existing session.
- The selected model provider is persisted per session and controls subsequent request routing.
- If no usable models are available, Codex is reported as unusable rather than falsely opening the Agents window.
- Provider account and model-catalog changes are reflected reactively.

## Acceptance criteria

- Signed out of GitHub + signed in to OpenAI/ChatGPT: Codex is usable.
- Signed out of GitHub + configured API-key/custom provider: Codex is usable.
- Copilot-backed Codex model without a GitHub token: authentication is requested on demand.
- No usable provider credentials: Codex does not count as an auth-free session type.
- Existing sessions retain their selected provider as other accounts sign in or out.
- Tests cover mixed provider inventories, model switching, session restoration, and each authentication matrix.

## Implementation

Addressed by #328461.

title: Agent Host fails to load user settings at startup
body:
## Description

When the Agent Host process starts, it attempts to initialize its configuration from a `vscode-userdata:` URI even though the process file service only registers the disk-backed `file:` provider. The configuration watcher consequently fails before Agent Host providers finish initializing.

This prevents Agent Host from loading the default profile's user settings, including network settings such as `http.proxy` that its request stack depends on.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start VS Code Insiders with Agent Host enabled.
2. Start or restore an Agent Host session.
3. Inspect `agenthost.log` immediately after process startup.

## Actual Behavior

Startup logs contain errors similar to:

```text
Agent Host process started successfully
CodeExpectedError: ENOPRO: No file system provider found for resource 'vscode-userdata:<user-data>/User'
CodeExpectedError: ENOPRO: No file system provider found for resource 'vscode-userdata:<user-data>/User/settings.json'
```

The Agent Host `ConfigurationService` is created with `environmentService.userRoamingDataHome`, whose scheme is `vscode-userdata`. The Agent Host entry points register `Schemas.file`, but do not register a `vscode-userdata` provider, so the settings file cannot be watched or loaded.

## Expected Behavior

Agent Host should load the default profile's disk-backed `User/settings.json` without file-system-provider errors so settings required by Agent Host services are available at startup.

## Related

- Related to #329116, which contains the same startup error while reporting missing Claude models after the first Remote SSH connection.
- Related to #328736, where the same startup error was observed while investigating disappearing Remote SSH sessions.

title: Expose large shell output artifact paths through the Copilot SDK
body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up from: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329720

When the Copilot runtime spills large shell output to a file, the tool completion text includes the saved-file path, while structured `shell_exit` content exposes only `outputPreview` and `outputTruncated`.

VS Code therefore has no typed way to surface or act on the full-output artifact. The immediate UI fix uses the tool completion display text when the structured preview is truncated, but deliberately does not parse a path out of that prose.

The public SDK/runtime contract should expose the large-output artifact location as structured shell completion data so consumers can render it without depending on presentation text.

Acceptance criteria:

- Add an optional structured artifact path or URI for spilled shell output to the runtime wire contract and generated public SDK types.
- Define enough lifetime/access semantics for an SDK consumer to know when the artifact can be opened.
- Update VS Code Agent Host to consume the structured value instead of relying on the tool completion display text.

title: Built-in skills cannot be disabled from the Customizations UI in the Agents window
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (`main`, found via source analysis)
- OS Version: N/A (platform-independent)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the **Agents** window.
2. Open the **Customizations** editor and select the **Skills** section.
3. Find a skill under the **Built-in** group and invoke **Disable** from its context menu.

**Expected:** the skill is shown as disabled and is no longer sent to the agent host.

**Actual:** nothing happens. The skill stays enabled in the list, and it is still bundled and sent to the agent host. The setting *is* persisted to storage — it just is never read back.

### Root cause

There are two independent "disabled" stores for customizations:

| Store | Storage key | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `IPromptsService.get/setDisabledPromptFiles(type)` | `chat.disabledPromptFiles.<type>` | the **Disable/Enable** actions in `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` |
| `AgentCustomizationSyncProvider.isDisabled(uri)` | `customizationSync.disabled.<harnessId>` | only `pluginListWidget.ts` (plugins) |

The Disable action writes to store #1, but the two places that matter in the Agents window read only store #2 (or neither):

1. `enumerateLocalCustomizationsForHarness` (`agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts`) computed `disabled` from `syncProvider.isDisabled(uri)` only, so a user-disabled built-in skill still made it into the synced bundle and was shipped to the agent host.
2. `SessionsCustomizationHarnessService` registers no built-in harnesses, so `isAgentHostTarget()` always matches in the Agents window and `aiCustomizationItemsModel` always selects `PureItemProviderItemSource`. That source built its list purely from the provider (i.e. from the bundle) and never consulted `getDisabledPromptFiles`.

Net effect: the Disable button rendered, wrote to storage, and nothing downstream ever read it.

### Notes for the fix

Both ends have to change together. Fixing only the bundling side makes a disabled built-in skill drop out of the bundle, so the provider stops reporting it and it **disappears from the Skills list entirely** — leaving no way to re-enable it, since the **Enable** menu item is gated on `disabled === true`. The item source must therefore also merge built-in skills in directly from the prompts service so they stay listed while disabled.

Related: #329753 (the two-store split that caused this).

title: Agents window: Support editor tab display modes in the single-pane layout
body:
## Description

The Agents window single-pane layout currently forces multiple editor tabs and does not integrate correctly with the `workbench.editor.showTabs` setting.

Support the setting without losing the Agents-specific editor header and Add Tab affordances:

- Respect `multiple` and `single` tab modes while the editor area is visible.
- Treat `none` as `single`, because the Agents window requires an editor title row.
- Use multiple tabs when only the docked Auxiliary Bar is visible so managed Changes and Files tabs remain directly accessible.
- Keep breadcrumbs in the Agents editor header, without duplicating the path in the single-tab title.
- Keep Add Tab before layout actions, using the standard toolbar trailing separator.
- In single-tab mode, keep all supported Add Tab entries available: Changes, Files, Browser, and Search.
- Preserve normal VS Code editor-window behavior.

## Verification steps

1. Enable `sessions.layout.singlePaneDetailPanel` and reload the Agents window.
2. Set `workbench.editor.showTabs` to `multiple`.
   - Verify the Agents side pane displays the normal multi-tab strip.
   - Verify the Add Tab menu is available and missing managed tabs can be reopened.
3. Set `workbench.editor.showTabs` to `single`.
   - Verify only the active editor title appears in the top row.
   - Verify the full-width Agents header remains in the row below.
   - Verify breadcrumbs appear only in the header and the path is not repeated beside the editor title.
   - Verify Add Tab appears before the layout actions with the standard toolbar separator after it.
   - Open Add Tab and verify Changes, Files, Browser, and Search are all listed even when their editors are already open.
4. Set `workbench.editor.showTabs` to `none`.
   - Verify the Agents window behaves as single-tab mode rather than hiding the title row.
5. Hide the editor area while keeping the docked Auxiliary Bar visible.
   - Verify the title switches to multiple tabs regardless of the configured tab mode.
   - Show the editor area again and verify the configured single/multiple behavior returns.
6. Open a regular VS Code editor window with `workbench.editor.showTabs` set to `single`.
   - Verify its existing single-tab title and inline breadcrumbs render normally, with no missing or duplicate header content.

title: Restore Agent Host request errors after a cold session reload
body:
## Feature request

When an Agent Host request fails, the error is visible while the session is live. After quitting and restarting VS Code, and reopening the session from persisted provider history, the failed turn should still display the same error.

Currently, persisted Copilot `session.error` events are not reconstructed into AHP error turns, so Copilot request failures disappear after a cold reload. Codex failed turns retain their status but do not restore the associated error details.

## Expected behavior

- Cold-restored Copilot sessions reconstruct persisted `session.error` events as terminal error turns.
- Errors preserve structured details used for quota, authentication, rate-limit, and provider error UI.
- Subagent errors restore on the corresponding subagent turn without changing the parent turn.
- Codex restores its natively persisted failed-turn error details.
- Live and replay paths use consistent error normalization.

Implemented by [#329828](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329828).

(Written by Copilot)

---

Verification steps

- Using both AH Copilot and Codex:
- Trigger an error in a session, eg start a Turn then disable wifi so it fails due to no network
- You see the error message
- Quit vscode, restart
- You still see the error message

title: Chat scroll position is lost when switching sessions
body:
When switching away from a chat session and then returning to it, the transcript resets to the bottom instead of restoring the previous scroll position. This makes it difficult to compare or continue reading earlier content across sessions.

Expected behavior:
- A transcript that was scrolled up restores its previous position.
- A transcript that was at the bottom remains pinned to the latest content.
- Behavior is consistent across the Chat panel, chat editor tabs, and the Agents window.

Draft fix: [#329844](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329844)

(Written by Copilot)

title: Internal reasoning text rendered below "Finished with N steps" in agent host + BYOK mode
body:
### Bug Description

In the **agent window** (agent host + Copilot CLI runtime), the model's internal reasoning text is rendered as visible content directly below the "Finished with N steps" collapsible section, with **each word on a separate line** (garbled formatting). Normal reply content follows after it.

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0-insider
- Mode: **agent mode (agent host + Copilot CLI 0.0.421)**
- Model: **DeepSeek V4 via the built-in BYOK channel** — configured in `chatLanguageModels.json` (`vendor: customendpoint`, `apiType: chat-completions`, `thinking: true`, `reasoningEffortFormat: chat-completions`), served by the built-in Copilot extension's `CustomEndpointBYOKModelProvider`. **No third-party extension is involved.**

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a DeepSeek reasoning model via `chatLanguageModels.json` (customendpoint / chat-completions).
2. Open the agent window and select the DeepSeek model.
3. Ask a question that triggers tool steps; continue a few turns.
4. Observe internal reasoning text rendered below "Finished with N steps", one word per line.

### Root-cause analysis

In agent host BYOK mode the chain is:

DeepSeek streaming `reasoning_content` → built-in BYOK provider emits one `LanguageModelThinkingPart` **per delta** (`extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/languageModelAccess.ts`) → `AgentHostByokLmHandler._appendReasoningOutput` merges them into a single reasoning item whose `summary` is an **array** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`) → `reasoningFrames()` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts` emits a **separate** `reasoning_summary_part.added → summary_text.delta → summary_text.done → part.done` SSE sequence **for every element** of the summary array.

This does not match the Responses API contract, where a single reasoning part receives streamed deltas. The CLI agent then renders each summary element as an individual reasoning line below the completion status — explaining the "one word per line" garbling.

title: [Perf] Agent Host listSessions spawns hundreds of Git processes
body:
## Summary

Reloading the Agents window can leave session details, especially change-summary counts, unavailable for tens of seconds while the local Agent Host handles its first `listSessions` request. During that interval the Agent Host can spawn hundreds of `git worktree list --porcelain` processes.

This regressed with [#328375](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328375), which added list-time repair for legacy worktree repository metadata. The repair is needed because archived sessions may never reopen through the normal `WorktreeIsolation` migration path, but it currently runs synchronously before `listSessions` returns.

## Root cause

List-time normalization uses two successful-result caches:

1. A session URI → normalized repository root cache in `AgentService`.
2. A checkout/worktree path → primary repository root cache in `PrimaryWorktreeRootResolver`.

Both caches were capped at 100 entries. A successful `git worktree list --porcelain` stores every worktree path returned by Git. For repositories with hundreds of linked worktrees, inserting one result immediately evicts most of the paths the result was intended to deduplicate. Later sessions miss the cache and spawn Git again.

The work is serialized, so the repeated process launches extend the `listSessions` critical path rather than running concurrently.

## Impact

### Captured slow reload

- Initial AHP `listSessions`: **52.2s**
- Copilot SDK enumeration: **2.6s** for 853 sessions
- Remaining Agent Host enrichment: approximately **49.6s**
- Distinct sampled `getWorktreeRoots → git spawn` invocations: **404**
- Result: 853 sessions, 833 change summaries, approximately 571KB

The renderer cannot display live change-summary counts until that response arrives. The late large update also causes visible renderer work, though multi-second GC pauses in the supplied trace were mostly trace-only V8 object-dump statistics.

### Controlled benchmark

A cold-start benchmark used fresh APFS copy-on-write clones of the same user-data profile on every run:

- 979 sessions
- 613 sessions with persisted worktree repository metadata
- New Code OSS and Agent Host process for each run

| Mode | Git processes | Worktree-normalization wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original 100-entry caches | 543–569 | **69–115s** |
| Caches sized to the catalog | 21–28 | **1.1–2.8s** (median 1.83s) |
| Skip list-time normalization | 0 | **0s** |

The original full `listSessions` request ranged from 55–122s. With catalog-sized caches, the benchmark median was approximately 14.7s, but whole-request time had substantial unrelated SDK/filesystem variability. The directly instrumented normalization barrier is the reliable comparison.

## Proposed fix

- Before list enrichment, ensure both normalization caches can retain at least the complete provider catalog.
- Keep successful resolution semantics and failure retry behavior unchanged.
- Persist the latest aggregate change counts in the existing renderer startup cache so recent session badges render before the live listing completes. Full changesets/diffs remain live-only.

This reduces list-time Git work to roughly one process per relevant repository and removes approximately 97–99% of the normalization cost.

## Follow-up opportunity

Even correctly cached normalization still costs approximately 1–3 seconds for this catalog. The compatibility migration could be moved off the synchronous listing path: return stored metadata immediately, repair legacy roots in t

title: SSH agent host ignores StrictHostKeyChecking yes/no because ssh -G emits true/false
body:
## Summary

SSH remote agent hosts ignore `StrictHostKeyChecking yes`, `no`, and `off` because `ssh -G` normalizes those values to `true` and `false`, while VS Code only recognizes the original spellings.

This is a follow-up to microsoft/vscode#329462 / microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8734. The host-key verification itself is working and fails safely, but the promised OpenSSH policy compatibility is incomplete.

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.133.0-insider`
- Commit: `5a36a9c68ce6300f94225aff5f8db533671af98b`
- Local OS: macOS `26.5.2` (`arm64`), system `/usr/bin/ssh`
- Also reproduced with OpenSSH `9.2p1` on Debian 12
- Extensions disabled: not applicable; this is the built-in SSH remote agent host

## Reproduction

1. Configure an SSH remote agent host with verification disabled:

   ```ssh-config
   Host host-key-test
       HostName 127.0.0.1
       Port 62222
       User node
       IdentityFile ~/.ssh/codespaces.auto
       StrictHostKeyChecking no
       UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null
   ```

2. Inspect the effective configuration:

   ```sh
   ssh -G host-key-test | grep -E '^(stricthostkeychecking|userknownhostsfile) '
   ```

   Output:

   ```text
   stricthostkeychecking false
   userknownhostsfile /dev/null
   ```

3. In the Agents window, run **Agents: Connect to Remote Agent Host via SSH** and select `host-key-test`.

4. VS Code prompts:

   ```text
   The authenticity of host 'host-key-test' can't be established.
   ```

   This is incorrect for `StrictHostKeyChecking no`.

Both macOS OpenSSH and Debian OpenSSH `9.2p1` produce this normalization matrix:

```text
yes        -> true
no         -> false
ask        -> ask
accept-new -> accept-new
off        -> false
```

## Root cause

`parseSSHGOutput` reads the normalized value emitted by `ssh -G` and passes it through `isSSHStrictHostKeyChecking`:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5a36a9c68ce6300f94225aff5f8db533671af98b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/sshConfigParsing.ts#L75-L88
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5a36a9c68ce6300f94225aff5f8db533671af98b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/sshRemoteAgentHost.ts#L263-L268

The accepted values are only:

```ts
'ask' | 'accept-new' | 'yes' | 'no' | 'off'
```

Therefore `true` and `false` become `undefined`. An unknown key then follows the default `ask` path instead of the user's configured policy.

## Expected behavior

Normalize effective OpenSSH boolean spellings before applying policy:

- `true` → `yes`
- `false` → `no` (equivalent to `off` for this policy)

The resulting behavior should remain:

- `yes`: reject an unknown key without prompting.
- `no` / `off`: accept an unknown key silently without persisting it.
- `ask`: prompt on an unknown key.
- `accept-new`: accept and persist an unknown key silently.
- Changed and revoked keys still hard-fail regardless of the `no` / `off` opt-out, as implemented by #329462.

## Impact

This is fail-closed rather than a security bypass: users receive an unexpected trust prompt. However, it means common OpenSSH configurations do not behave as configured, and the `StrictHostKeyChecking` compatibility added by #329462 cannot currently be verified for `yes`, `no`, or `off`.

GitHub Codespaces configurations generated by `gh codespace ssh --config` use `StrictHostKeyChecking no`, so this is readily observable when connecting a Codespace through an SSH transport.

## Suggested tests

- Add `parseSSHGOutput` cases for `stricthostkeychecking true` and `false`.
- Cover all fi

title: Agent Host logs an error when a local commit is not on GitHub
body:
The Agent Host pull-request lookup added in #329825 treats GitHub's expected `422 No commit found for SHA` response as an operational failure when the current local commit has not been pushed. This produces both an error and a follow-up warning in the Agent Host log:

```text
2026-08-10 10:02:40.745 [error] [AgentHostOctoKit] GET https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/vscode/commits/4ec191d238f0d4f2d0186abfa1f41f6f521c52c0/pulls?per_page=100 - Status: 422 - {"message":"No commit found for SHA: 4ec191d238f0d4f2d0186abfa1f41f6f521c52c0","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit","status":"422"}
2026-08-10 10:02:40.746 [warning] [AgentHostGitStateService][attachSessionGitHubPullRequest] Failed to find pull request for copilotcli:/fc37d4b5-f896-46fa-afb9-7fdcf3934c92 GitHub API request failed: GET repos/microsoft/vscode/commits/4ec191d238f0d4f2d0186abfa1f41f6f521c52c0/pulls?per_page=100 - 422 Unprocessable Entity - {"message":"No commit found for SHA: 4ec191d238f0d4f2d0186abfa1f41f6f521c52c0","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit","status":"422"}
```

An unpushed/local-only commit cannot have a GitHub pull request, so this response should be handled as a normal “no pull request found” result for the commit lookup. Other GitHub API failures should continue to surface.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Chat input notices: unify under one base widget and one stylesheet
body:
Follow-up to #329284, which unified the *behaviour* of the five notices above a chat input (one arbitration host decides what shows). It deliberately left the *presentation* alone. This issue covers the second half: one base class and one stylesheet.

## Problem

Five producers compete for the space above a chat input. After #329284 they all speak one arbitration protocol, but they are still built and styled five different ways:

| Producer | Rendered by |
| --- | --- |
| Notification | `ChatInputNotificationWidget` (own class) |
| Voice introduction | `VoiceModeOnboardingBanner` → `ChatInputOnboardingCard` |
| Dictation introduction | `DictationOnboardingBanner` → `ChatInputOnboardingCard` |
| Getting-started tip | `ChatTipContentPart` (a chat *content part*) |
| Sub-session tip | raw `dom.$()` calls, no class at all |

The only thing all five share is `IChatInputNoticeFocusTarget` (`hasFocus`/`focus`/`canFocus`) — a focus contract, not a rendering one.

## This is not just tidying — they visibly disagree

Container chrome is duplicated across four stylesheets, and the same visual role is expressed at different token tiers:

| | Radius | Background | Border |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Voice card | `cornerRadius-large` → `xSmall` | `agentsChatInput-background` | `--vscode-strokeThickness` |
| Dictation card | `cornerRadius-large` → `xSmall` | `agentsChatInput-background` | `--vscode-strokeThickness` |
| Chat tip | `cornerRadius-small` → `0` | `editorWidget-background` | hardcoded `1px` |
| Sub-session tip | `cornerRadius-small` → `0` | `editorWidget-background` | hardcoded `1px` |
| Notification | `cornerRadius-small` (top only) | `color-mix(severity)` | hardcoded `1px` |

Voice and dictation are byte-identical except one padding token. Chat tip and sub-session tip are near-identical copy-paste. Two of the five use a raw `1px` where the others use the stroke token.

Chrome blocks to collapse:
- `chatInputNotificationWidget.css:16`
- `voiceModeOnboarding.css:35`
- `dictationOnboarding.css:37`
- `chatTipContent.css:58`
- `newChatInSession.css:125`

## Proposal

1. Generalize the existing `ChatInputOnboardingCard` (`chatInputOnboarding.ts:319`) into a `ChatInputNoticeWidget` base: container chrome, ARIA region + label, `IChatInputNoticeFocusTarget` implementation, standard dismiss action, and the `setVisible` suspend/resume hook added in #329284.
2. Add one `chatInputNotice.css` with a single chrome rule plus modifiers for the three legitimate variants (onboarding card / tip / notification severity).
3. Migrate all five producers and delete the duplicated chrome.
4. Reconcile the token disagreements above — one radius ramp, one background role, `--vscode-strokeThickness` everywhere.

## Estimated size

**~+350 / −200 across ~12 files.**

| Work | Lines |
| --- | --- |
| Generalize card → `ChatInputNoticeWidget` | +100 |
| Single `chatInputNotice.css` | +80 |
| Delete 5 duplicated chrome blocks | −70 |
| Sub-session tip: raw DOM → base class (`newChatInSessionWidget.ts:99`) | −25 |
| Notification migration (`chatInputNotificationWidget.ts:89`) — hand-rolls header/title/actions the card already provides | ~40 changed |
| Voice + dictation migration (already on the card, mostly renames) | ~20 changed |
| Chat tip migration (`chatTipContentPart.ts:31`) — a `ChatContentPart`, different lifecycle, the awkward one | ~40 changed |
| Base class tests | +80 |

title: Chat input stack: make the notice/input seam structural instead of per-surface offsets
body:
Follow-up to #330307, which unified how the five notices above a chat input *look* (one base widget, one stylesheet). That change deliberately left one thing alone, and this issue is about fixing it properly: **how far each notice sits from the input below it.**

## Problem

A notice has a square bottom edge; the chat input has rounded top corners. Sat flush, the input's rounding leaves gaps at the corners and the two borders read as a seam. So each surface pulls the input up over the notice's bottom edge to hide the join.

The number is different everywhere. Measured against `main`:

| offset | surface |
| --- | --- |
| −8px | sessions homepage, notification |
| −6px | workbench panel, notification |
| −4px | workbench compact, getting-started tip |
| 0 | workbench panel tip, sessions tip, sub-session tip |
| +4px | voice and dictation introductions |
| +16px | inline chat, notification (a deliberate gap) |

The reason it cannot be one value is structural: **the notices are not adjacent to the input.** The flat layout puts thirteen slots above it, four of which sit *between* the last notice and the input:

```
… → notification → voice → dictation → goal-banner → todo-list
  → artifacts → editing-session → getting-started-tip → INPUT
```

So which widget actually touches the input depends on which ones are present. The current answer is adjacency arithmetic: **11 negative margins across 7 stylesheets**, each widget squaring its own corners, plus a five-selector `:has()` block in `chat.css` that squares the input's top whenever any of five widgets appears.

That block also conflicts with our own guidance — `.github/instructions/css-best-practices.instructions.md` says to avoid `:has()` and use an explicit marker class instead.

### Sharing the offset does not work, and has now failed twice

Both attempts happened during #330307 and were reverted:

1. A shared offset on the notice lane **slipped past existing per-surface overrides**, which only ever set `margin-bottom`, leaving 10px of dead space in two surfaces.
2. Splitting a hide/show pair across two files produced **equally specific rules**, so whichever stylesheet loaded last won, and the voice card could render `display: none`.

The lesson is that the offset is not a property of the notice at all. It is a property of the stack it sits in.

## Proposal

One container holds every above-input widget **and** the input:

- `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0`
- the border and the radius live on the **container**, with `overflow: hidden`
- children draw no radius and no adjoining border of their own

Then the seam disappears structurally. No negative margins, no corner-squaring rules, no presence checks. Adding or removing a widget is automatic, and the eight widget families stop needing to know about each other.

## How this works if notices appear outside the input

Worth stating explicitly, because it shapes the design.

Two of the three layers already generalise:

- **Arbitration.** `ChatInputNoticeHubService` is already a window-level registry: it holds a set of hosts, tracks recency, and routes focus to whichever is active. Each area gets a host; lanes and claims are per-host. Nothing here assumes an input.
- **Appearance.** `.chat-input-notice` already describes what a notice looks like independently of where it is docked.

The part that does **not** generalise today is the seam assumption baked into the shared frame: `border-bottom: none` plus squared bottom corners ass

title: Child-process IPC cleanup creates an unhandled rejection when a request fails
body:
When a child-process IPC request rejects, `Client.requestPromise` attaches cleanup with `result.finally(...)` and ignores the promise returned by `finally`. Even when the caller handles the original rejection, the cleanup branch rejects without a handler and is reported as an unhandled promise rejection.

## Reproduction on Insiders

This was observed on VS Code Insiders 1.134.0, commit `f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1`, on Windows.

1. Open a local folder in VS Code Insiders.
2. Start an Agent Host-backed agent session so that the Agent Host file monitor is active.
3. Run **Developer: Open Process Explorer**.
4. Locate the Agent Host child process whose command line contains `--type=fileWatcher`, right-click it, and select **Force Kill Process** while the agent session is active.
5. Run **Developer: Open Logs Folder** and inspect `main.log`.

The native watcher crash that exposed this may not reproduce consistently, but terminating the child process exercises the same IPC cancellation path.

## Actual

The watcher is restarted, but Agent Host stderr also reports a duplicate unhandled cancellation rejection:

```text
[AgentHost:stderr] IPC "File Watcher" crashed with exit code 3221225477 and signal null
[AgentHost:stderr] Unhandled Promise Rejection: Canceled: Canceled
```

The rejection stack originates from cancellation while disposing active requests in the child-process IPC exit handler.

## Expected

The original IPC request still rejects so its caller can handle the error, but the internal cleanup branch does not create a second unhandled rejection.

## Root cause

`result.finally(cleanup)` creates a new promise that mirrors `result`'s rejection. Because that new promise is ignored, any rejected IPC request can surface globally even if the returned original promise is handled. Cleanup needs fulfillment and rejection handlers while preserving and returning the original promise.

The native file watcher access violation is separate; this issue tracks the deterministic unhandled rejection produced while processing a child-process exit.

title: Surface failing CI sessions in Omni Chat
body:
## Feature request

Surface agent sessions with failing pull-request CI in the Omni Chat window, alongside the existing sessions that need questions answered or tool actions approved.

## Proposed experience

- Include failing-CI sessions in Omni's existing attention panel/carousel below the input.
- Prioritize questions and approvals before CI failures.
- Show the affected session title and failed/pending check counts.
- Provide a prominent **Fix CI** action.
- Run the fix in the affected session in the background without opening or focusing that session.
- Optimistically remove the card after requesting a fix.
- Resurface the session only when a new head SHA has failing checks.

## Clearing behavior

Clear only the affected session, not the entire carousel:

- Remove it immediately when **Fix CI** is activated.
- Remove it while any new request for that session is in progress.
- Keep it hidden for the current head after a successful Fix CI submission.
- If a different request completes without fixing or acknowledging the current failing head, allow the CI card to reappear.
- Leave unrelated questions, approvals, and CI failures in the carousel.

## Eligibility

Match the Agents window behavior:

- The session is not archived or in progress.
- The associated pull request is open and not a draft.
- CI has at least one failing check.
- A fix has not already been requested for the current head SHA.

## Implementation considerations

- Reuse the existing `BlockedSessions` and `BlockedSessionsCIFixModel` behavior rather than duplicating GitHub polling, prompt construction, or background submission.
- Preserve the `workbench`/`sessions` layer boundary through a narrow provider API owned by Omni.
- Preserve carousel selection across reactive updates.
- Do not load a session chat model merely to display its CI status.
- Keep the **Fix CI** control stable while check counts update so keyboard focus is preserved.
- Use localized, accessible status text and existing orange CI action styling.

## Acceptance criteria

- Failing CI sessions appear reactively in Omni with accurate failed/pending counts.
- Questions and approvals remain higher priority.
- **Fix CI** submits once in the background and removes the current occurrence.
- Passing, draft, closed, archived, in-progress, and already-fixed current-head sessions do not appear.
- A subsequent failing head SHA appears as a new occurrence.
- Existing Omni routing, voice activation, pending prompts, focus behavior, and window sizing are unchanged.

body:

title: Markdown Editor: expose a command to toggle Editing / Locked mode
body:
## Feature request

Please expose the existing **Editing / Locked** mode toggle in the Markdown Editor (`vscode.markdown.editor`) as a VS Code command that can be assigned in Keyboard Shortcuts / `keybindings.json`.

A default keybinding is not required. A command for toggling the mode of the active Markdown Editor would be enough.

## Motivation

I frequently switch between reading and editing rendered Markdown.

In **Editing** mode, clicking a rendered block reveals its Markdown syntax and can change the document layout. When I am mainly reading or reviewing a document, I prefer **Locked** mode because the rendered view stays stable.

However, switching between Editing and Locked currently requires using the mode toggle in the UI.

The toggle itself can be reached through keyboard focus navigation, but there is no dedicated VS Code command that I can bind directly to a shortcut.

This is also useful in the Agents window, where range-based Agent Feedback is available in Locked mode, so my workflow often becomes:

```text
Editing
  ↓
Locked
  ↓
Editing
```

Being able to switch directly from the keyboard would make this workflow much smoother.

## Current behavior

- The Markdown Editor has a UI toggle for Editing / Locked.
- I could not find a dedicated VS Code command for this mode toggle.
- `markdown.preview.toggleLock` controls the existing Markdown Preview and does not toggle the Markdown Editor's Editing / Locked mode.
- `workbench.action.files.toggleActiveEditorReadonlyInSession` controls the file-level read-only state and is separate from the Markdown Editor's Editing / Locked mode.
- #329414 registers Markdown Editor commands as VS Code commands so that their shortcuts can be customized, but the Editing / Locked toggle is not currently exposed as one of these commands.

## Expected behavior

Expose a command that toggles the active Markdown Editor between Editing and Locked mode.

For example (command name only illustrative):

```text
markdown.editor.toggleLocked
```

Users could then assign any keybinding they prefer.

## Related

- #326250 — Markdown Editor Editing / read-only mode UI toggle
- #327538 — Revealing Markdown markers can shift content while editing
- #326539 — Agent Feedback is offered in Locked mode
- #329414 — Markdown Editor commands can now be customized with shortcuts

title: Support auto model selection in .agent.md based on task complexity
body:
## Summary

Allow custom agents () to declare a **model selection policy** instead of (or in addition to) a static model, so VS Code can pick the best available model for each invocation based on task complexity, context size, or tool requirements.

## Problem

Currently, custom agents pin a single model (or a static fallback array) in frontmatter:

This creates a hard trade-off:

| Scenario | Static model choice | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Simple refactor ("add a type annotation") | Expensive / large model | Wastes tokens and money |
| Complex architecture analysis | Cheap / small model | Poor quality, misses nuance |
| High-tool-calling task (CI, k8s manifests) | Model without reliable tool calling | Fails silently or hallucinates tool args |
| Long-context summarization | Small-context model | Truncates, loses critical info |

Multi-agent setups amplify this: an orchestrator dispatches to 5+ phase agents, each hardcoded to one model. The orchestrator cannot adapt model selection to the workload it's handing off.

## Proposed solution

Add a  (or ) frontmatter field alongside :

### How  selection would work

1. VS Code already knows each model's capabilities from  (tool calling, vision, max tokens, context window).
2. At invocation time, the agent framework inspects the user's request + tool set + conversation context length.
3. It selects the cheapest model whose capabilities satisfy the policy constraints.
4. If no model qualifies, fall back to the explicit  list or the  field.

### Capability-aware selection signals

| Signal | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Tool calling required | Agent's  list is non-empty | Filter to models with  |
| Large context | Conversation history + attachments > 64K tokens | Filter to models with  ≥ context size |
| Vision needed | User attached image(s) | Filter to models with  |
| Task complexity | User prompt heuristic (code analysis, multi-file refactor, architecture) | Prefer larger models when quality-first; smaller when cost-optimal |

- **Cost**: Users with BYOK endpoints (token-plan models, self-hosted) pay per token. Routing trivial tasks to a 1M-context model is wasteful.
- **Quality**: Complex tasks on small models degrade the agent experience silently — the agent works but produces shallow output.
- **Orchestrator workflows**: Multi-agent setups (DE → SE → EM pattern, or CI pipeline agents) need per-task model selection. The orchestrator knows the phase but can't express it in the current model field.
- **Provider diversity**: As more BYOK providers are added (LM Studio, cloud endpoints, token plans), the selection problem grows combinatorially.

title: Same-name user/workspace MCP collision leaves stopped server inoperable until server ID is renamed
body:
## Summary

In a multi-repository workspace, defining the same MCP server ID in multiple
repository `.vscode/mcp.json` files and in the user-scoped `mcp.json` left one
deterministic but stopped/inoperable server entry. Temporarily renaming only
the user-scoped server ID restored MCP CodeLens immediately and allowed the
server to be started and authenticated from Agent Customizations.

This reproduces on an Insiders build that includes the same-name ordering fix
from #327979 / #329010, so it may be a remaining stale
registration/activation case after a collision winner is selected.

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.135.0-insider`
- Commit: `05bf4f5ce25799e2d0daf32bf90cb885ca75a0b9`
- Date: `2026-08-20T04:40:55Z`
- OS: macOS
- Surface: Agent Host and **Agent Customizations > MCP Servers**
- Server: Figma remote HTTP MCP (`https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`)

## Configuration

Multiple repositories in the workspace and the user configuration used the
same conventional server ID:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "figma": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

This is a normal setup for us: repositories carry team-owned MCP
configuration, while the user entry makes the same server available in
repositories that do not provide it.

## Observed behavior

1. `MCP: List Servers` showed one `figma` entry in a stopped state, pointing to
   one repository `.vscode/mcp.json`.
2. Starting or restarting that entry from the Command Palette was ineffective.
3. The colliding `mcp.json` did not show the MCP **Start/Configure** CodeLens,
   so the server could not be started from the file either.
4. Agent Host sessions did not receive Figma tools.
5. Window output logged a collision:

   ```text
   Overwriting mcp server 'figma' from <workspace-folder>/.vscode/mcp.json
   with <user-profile>/User/mcp.json.
   ```

## Recovery observation

1. I renamed only the user-scoped key from `figma` to `figma-user`.
2. The MCP CodeLens appeared immediately, without a window reload.
3. Starting the renamed entry initially remained at `Starting...`.
4. Starting it from **Agent Customizations > MCP Servers** subsequently
   surfaced the expected external Figma OAuth flow and completed successfully.
5. Renaming the user entry back to `figma` did not immediately reproduce the
   failure.

`MCP: Reset Trust` was also used earlier during troubleshooting, so it may have
affected the eventual OAuth flow. However, the immediate return of CodeLens
was directly correlated with changing the server ID.

## Expected behavior

- Same-name user/workspace entries should resolve through deterministic
  collision priority.
- The effective winner should remain startable through `MCP: List Servers`,
  its configuration CodeLens, and Agent Customizations.
- Replacing or shadowing a definition should fully invalidate stale server
  registration, lifecycle, and session tool-projection state.
- Users should not need to coordinate globally unique server names across
  private user configuration and team-owned repository configuration.

## Possible area to investigate

Changing the key may have created a new internal server identity and forced
registration, CodeLens, activation, or authentication bindings to be rebuilt.
The state shown by the Window registry, `MCP: List Servers`, CodeLens, Agent
Customizations, and the Agent Host session appeared inconsistent before that
rename.

title: Remote agent-host sync drops a skill's sibling references/ files, breaking Markdown links from SKILL.md
body:
**Describe the bug**

When a skill's `SKILL.md` links to a sibling file (e.g. `references/rules.md`) via a relative Markdown link, and the session is connected to a **remote host** (e.g. Remote-SSH), the linked file is missing after sync. The skill loads and its frontmatter/body are usable, but attempting to follow the link to the reference file fails because that file was never copied to the remote.

This appears to be because the agent-host sync path (`resolveCustomizationRefs` in `agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts`, backed by `SyncedCustomizationBundler` in `syncedCustomizationBundler.ts`) enumerates a skill as a single loose file keyed on the `SKILL.md` URI (`ISyncableFile`), and bundles only that exact URI into the synthetic remote plugin — it never resolves or copies files the `SKILL.md` links to via relative Markdown paths. On the local/extension-host path this isn't a problem because the whole containing folder stays on disk and relative links resolve naturally (see discussion in #304721), but the remote-sync path only materializes the one bundled file.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a local skill folder: `~/.copilot/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md` (or the equivalent user skills location) containing a relative link, e.g. `[more info](./references/notes.md)`, plus `~/.copilot/skills/my-skill/references/notes.md`.
2. Open a Remote-SSH window connected to a remote host.
3. Start an agent/chat session on the remote and invoke the skill so it loads.
4. Inspect the synced skill's base directory on the remote (under the `vscode-synced-customization-*` cache in the remote `agentPlugins` data folder) — only `SKILL.md` is present; `references/notes.md` is missing.
5. Ask the agent to follow the link — it cannot, since the file doesn't exist at that path on the remote.

**Expected behavior**
Files referenced via relative Markdown links from a synced `SKILL.md` (per the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification#file-references)) should be resolved and included in the remote bundle, the same way they work when the skill is loaded from a local extension/plugin folder.

**Related issues**
- #291388 (same underlying symptom, but the reporter tested locally rather than over a remote connection, which is likely why it couldn't be reproduced)
- #304721 (adjacent: confirms relative-linked supporting files are expected to work, in the extension-contribution context)

title: Add telemetry for pinning and unpinning chat models
body:
We currently have no telemetry for pinning or unpinning models in Chat.

Pin/unpin is stored locally (`chatModelPinned` in profile storage). `LanguageModelsService.pinModel()` / `unpinModel()` update that storage and fire `_onDidChangePinnedModels`, but they do not log an event. The model picker Pin Model / Unpin Model action (`modelPickerWidget` → `onTogglePin`) and the same action in the Models editor (`chatModelsWidget`) both go through that path with no `publicLog`.

Existing picker events do **not** cover this:
- `chat.modelchange` fires when a model is **selected**
- `chat.modelpickerinteraction` covers expand/collapse Other Models, premium upgrade, and contact-admin — not pin/unpin

### Proposal

Log telemetry when a user pins or unpins a model, including at least:
- Action: pin vs unpin
- Model identifier (and vendor if available, consistent with `chat.modelchange` — Copilot vendor only / non-Copilot as `unknown` if that is the privacy pattern)

title: Sandbox bypass confirmation should offer disabling sandbox for the session
body:
When the Copilot SDK requests a sandbox bypass, VS Code currently presents its standard tool-confirmation options. The existing **Allow in this Session** choice remembers tool approval; it does not disable sandboxing for the session. As a result, users must confirm each command that legitimately cannot run inside the sandbox.

The Copilot App offers a clearer set of choices:

- Cancel
- Run once outside sandbox
- Disable sandbox and run

VS Code should offer the equivalent session-scoped choice when all of the following are true:

- The Copilot Runtime marks the request as a sandbox bypass.
- Sandboxing is enabled for the current session.
- Enterprise policy allows sandbox bypass.

Suggested wording: **Disable sandbox for this session and run**.

Selecting it should:

1. Approve the current command outside the sandbox.
2. Disable sandboxing only for the current session.
3. Keep the user's saved sandbox setting unchanged.
4. Make the session's unsandboxed state visible in the permissions UI.
5. Avoid offering the choice when managed policy sets `sandbox.allowBypass` to `false`.

This should be a sandbox-specific option rather than reusing **Allow in this Session**. The latter changes tool approval for future calls; it does not communicate or implement the broader security posture change of disabling containment for the rest of the session.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: Chat: editing text before an inline #file: reference deletes the reference
body:
Type: Bug

### Summary

In the **unsubmitted** chat input, editing text *before* an inline `#file:` reference makes the workbench **delete the reference text itself**. This is not the keyboard removing an attachment chip — `chatDynamicVariableModel` actively calls `executeEdits(..., text: "")` on the reference range.

This is distinct from #281766 (editing an *already submitted* prompt, closed/completed) and #284059 (ghost decorations left behind). Here the input has never been submitted.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Chat.
2. Type a sentence, e.g. `Compare the ownership section of` .
3. Type `#`, pick a file from the picker so `#file:BACKLOG.md` is inserted inline, then continue typing `with the current draft.`
4. Move the caret **before** the reference (into the earlier part of the sentence) and edit there — e.g. press `Backspace` at the position immediately preceding the reference, or delete/retype a word right in front of it.

### Expected

The reference keeps tracking its text. Editing unrelated text earlier in the prompt must not affect it.

### Actual

The `#file:BACKLOG.md` text is removed from the input entirely, and the variable is dropped from the model. The user must re-open the picker and re-insert it.

### Why this matters

Inline references are the only mechanism that puts context **at a specific position in the sentence**. That positional placement is the whole point: it lets you write "compare `#file:a.md` against `#file:b.md`" instead of relying on pronouns and hoping the model binds them to the right attachment chips. Attachment chips are not a substitute — they carry no position. So losing an inline reference during ordinary editing is not a cosmetic glitch; it silently degrades the prompt into ambiguous demonstratives, and the loss is easy to miss because only the highlight disappears.

### Root cause

`chatDynamicVariableModel._subscribeToEditor()` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/contrib/chatDynamicVariables.ts`), in the `onDidChangeModelContent` handler:

```js
if (model.getValueInRange(decorationRange) !== data.text) {
  const change = e.changes.find(c =>
    c.rangeOffset <= data.rangeOffset &&
    c.rangeOffset + c.rangeLength >= data.rangeOffset + data.text.length);   // must FULLY ENCLOSE the ref
  const newRange = change && this.findReferenceRangeInReplacement(model, e.changes, change, data);
  return newRange
    ? { ...ref, range: newRange }
    : (change || this.widget.inputEditor.executeEdits(this.id, [{ range: decorationRange, text: '' }]),
       toDispose.push(ref), null);
}
```

The recovery path (`findReferenceRangeInReplacement`) is only attempted when a change **fully encloses** the reference. An edit *before* the reference does not enclose it, so `change` is `undefined` and control falls to the `else` branch, which deletes the reference text and drops the variable.

An edit before the reference reaches this branch at all only because the decoration range no longer yields the exact reference text — decoration stickiness lets an edit adjacent to the reference boundary grow or shift the range, so `getValueInRange(decorationRange) !== data.text` becomes true even though the reference itself was untouched.

### Suggested fix

Deleting the user's text should not be the fallback for "I lost track of this range". Either:

1. Widen the recovery to handle changes that merely *precede* the reference (recompute the offset from the change delta and re-anchor), or
2. When recovery fails, drop the va

title: Icons render as missing glyphs in Remote-SSH since 1.136.0 — glicons.woff2 fails to load
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Effectively yes for *other* extensions — reproduced on a clean isolated VS Code Insiders (zip/side-by-side, separate settings & extensions store per official FAQ), with **only `ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh` installed** to establish the Remote-SSH session. No other user extensions present in that profile. The tofu icons still occur. (Can additionally run "Disable All Installed Extensions" in that Insiders profile if the team wants the literal state.)

- VS Code Version: 1.136.0 (commit 520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1, also reproduced on 1.137.0-insiders zip)
- OS Version: Local: Windows 11 (system setup, Electron 42.10.0), Remote: Linux (Ubuntu/Rocky, x86_64)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code 1.136.0 (or 1.137.0-insiders zip) and connect to any remote host via Remote-SSH (only the `ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh` extension is installed; no other user extensions present).
2. Observe activity bar / status bar icons — multiple unrelated extensions (GitLens, Trae, etc.) render as missing glyphs (box with "×" in 1.136.0, empty box in 1.137.0-insiders). Tooltips on hover still work correctly.
3. Open Developer Tools (Help > Toggle Developer Tools > Console) and observe: `glicons.woff2?author…eme=vscode-remote:1 Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FAILED`

---

**Additional Context:**

- **Local windows are completely unaffected** — only Remote-SSH sessions exhibit the issue.
- **Version comparison:**
  - 1.135.0: ✅ Icons render correctly
  - 1.136.0: ❌ Icons render as box with ×
  - 1.137.0-insiders: ❌ Icons render as empty box
- **Troubleshooting already performed:**
  - `Developer: Reload Window` — no effect
  - Deleted `~/.vscode-server` entirely and reconnected (server re-downloaded from scratch) — issue persists
  - Reinstalled affected extensions in remote scope — no effect
  - `View: Reset View Locations` — no effect
- **Cross-checked with an isolated Insiders profile** (which does not share the Stable extension set) — similar missing glyphs with only Remote-SSH present. This makes a "some other installed extension breaks icon font" theory unlikely, since the broken surface is the shared product-icon font under the `vscode-remote` theme, not any single extension's own icons.
- **Suspected area (not confirmed):** given that local windows are unaffected, only `vscode-remote`-themed surfaces break, and the failing resource is `glicons.woff2?…theme=vscode-remote:1`, this *looks like* a regression in how the remote product icon font is addressed/loaded since 1.136.0 — but I haven't traced the webview/font loader yet; treat as lead, not conclusion.

title: Windows: CLI plugin discovery watchers block plugin install, update, and uninstall
body:
## Type of issue

Bug in VS Code's discovery of plugins installed by the GitHub Copilot CLI.

Upstream report: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4095
Related duplicate: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4151
Introducing VS Code change: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/314805

## Problem

On Windows, GitHub Copilot CLI plugin install, update, and uninstall can fail with:

```text
Failed to install plugin: Error: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

The upstream investigation enumerated open handles and found VS Code's file-watcher utility holding `ReadDirectoryChangesW`-style handles on the CLI-installed plugin root and component directories such as `hooks`, `agents`, and `skills`. Closing all VS Code windows releases the handles and the same CLI operation succeeds immediately.

## VS Code causal chain

`CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery` scans:

```text
~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/
```

It watches each marketplace directory and treats every immediate child directory as a plugin source, including CLI staging directories named like:

```text
.<plugin>.tmp-<pid>-0
```

The shared `AbstractAgentPluginDiscovery` then creates non-recursive watchers on:

- the plugin root
- `commands`
- `skills`
- `agents`
- `hooks`
- other resolved component paths

Relevant code:

- CLI discovery and marketplace bucket watchers: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/agentPluginServiceImpl.ts`
- Plugin root and component watchers: `AbstractAgentPluginDiscovery._toPlugin` in the same file
- Windows watcher backend: `src/vs/platform/files/node/watcher/parcel/parcelWatcher.ts`

This causes two related failure modes:

1. **Fresh installs can fail intermittently.** For sufficiently large plugins, VS Code discovers the staging directory and opens watcher handles before the CLI performs its final rename. Small plugins can finish the rename before discovery reacts, making the bug appear size- or plugin-dependent.
2. **Updates and uninstalls can fail consistently.** VS Code already has persistent watcher handles inside the final installed directory. The CLI cannot atomically rename/replace that directory on Windows, and VS Code cannot observe the successful parent-directory change that would cause it to rebuild or dispose those watchers.

The handle paths reported upstream match the watchers created by `AbstractAgentPluginDiscovery` exactly.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, install a Copilot CLI plugin under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/...`.
2. Open VS Code with Copilot/plugin discovery active and confirm the plugin is discovered.
3. While VS Code remains open, run:

   ```text
   copilot plugin update <plugin>@<marketplace>
   ```

   The same problem can affect `plugin install` and `plugin uninstall`.
4. Observe `Access is denied. (os error 5)` during the final directory rename/replacement.
5. Close VS Code and repeat the operation; it succeeds.

## Expected behavior

VS Code should allow the CLI to atomically install, replace, or remove CLI-owned plugin directories while still reflecting changes without requiring a reload.

## Suggested direction

Avoid placing persistent watcher handles inside CLI-owned plugin directories. For example:

- watch the installed-plugins root or marketplace buckets from an ancestor, preferably recursively;
- use ancestor events to invalidate and rediscover affected plugins;
- do not create plugin-root/component watchers for `CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery` sources;
- excl

title: Managed Settings: add smoketest coverage
body:
> Establish a migration safety net proving standard VS Code policy, the legacy
> Copilot-policy bridge, and direct managed settings produce the expected
> behavior and compose restrictively.

## Problem

VS Code has focused tests for policy and managed-settings components, but no
product smoke test proving that standard VS Code policy, legacy Copilot policy,
and Enterprise Managed Settings reach the expected client/runtime behavior.

## Proposed coverage

| Case | Path | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Standard non-chat policy | VS Code policy service | A conflicting user setting is overridden, locked, and visible in Policy Diagnostics |
| Legacy Copilot policy | VS Code policy → compatibility bridge → SDK/runtime | Shell approval and domain restrictions are enforced |
| Managed settings | Managed-settings resolution → SDK/runtime | Equivalent shell and domain restrictions are enforced |
| Mixed migration case | Legacy policy + managed settings | Sources compose toward the more restrictive result |

## Checklist

- [ ] Add an isolated `Policy Plumbing` suite under `test/smoke`.
- [ ] Cover one safe non-chat policy such as `ExtensionsAutoUpdate="off"`.
- [ ] Run one deterministic shell/domain scenario through the legacy policy path.
- [ ] Run the same scenario through equivalent managed settings.
- [ ] Assert Policy Diagnostics reports the expected source in each case.
- [ ] Assert denied operations never execute and the agent session remains usable.
- [ ] Add the mixed-source composition case after the parity cases are stable.
- [ ] Isolate policy state and `COPILOT_CACHE_HOME` between variants.

<details>
<summary>Implementation pointers</summary>

title: GitHub Authentication: Support expiring GitHub tokens brokered through Microsoft Entra
body:
## Problem

The GitHub Authentication extension can broker GitHub access tokens through a signed-in Microsoft Entra account. These exchanged GitHub tokens have a finite lifetime, but the extension previously treated them like ordinary persisted GitHub OAuth tokens with no known expiry or renewal path.

Once an exchanged token expired, consumers could lose authentication and fall back to an interactive sign-in prompt even though the Microsoft account was still signed in and could silently mint a replacement.

## Desired behavior

- Keep the exchanged token's absolute expiry internally.
- Return its current relative lifetime through `AuthenticationSession.expiresIn`.
- Recompute the remaining lifetime whenever a cached session is returned.
- Silently renew Microsoft-brokered GitHub sessions before expiry, including the one-hour threshold required by the Copilot SDK.
- Coalesce concurrent renewal attempts.
- Retain a still-valid token when proactive renewal fails transiently, and only remove the session after the token actually expires.
- Leave ordinary persisted GitHub OAuth sessions unchanged when their expiry is unknown.

## Implementation

Implemented by #334418, including mocked coverage for initial exchange, restore, cached lifetime recomputation, renewal, and transient renewal failures.

title: API proposal: Expose AuthenticationSession access token lifetime
body:
## Problem

`AuthenticationSession` exposes an access token but not its lifetime. Consumers that integrate with SDKs supporting renewable credentials cannot tell whether a token is static or when it should be refreshed.

#152517 previously proposed exposing an absolute `expiresAt` timestamp. An absolute timestamp is unsafe across VS Code's client/remote extension-host boundary because the two machines may have clock skew.

## Proposed API

```ts
export interface AuthenticationSession {
	/**
	 * The access token's remaining lifetime, in seconds, when the authentication provider returns the session.
	 *
	 * This corresponds to `expires_in` in an OAuth 2.0 token response. Providers returning
	 * cached sessions must recompute this value. This is undefined when the authentication
	 * provider does not know the access token's expiry. When defined, this must be a positive integer.
	 */
	readonly expiresIn?: number;
}
```

## Semantics

- The value is a positive integer representing whole seconds remaining when the session is returned.
- Cached sessions recompute the value on every return.
- `undefined` means the provider does not know the token's expiry.
- The relative lifetime avoids comparing clocks across extension-host boundaries.

## Implementation

The proposed declaration and first consumer are implemented experimentally in #334418 under `vscode.proposed.authSessionExpiration.d.ts`.

Related to #152517.
