title: Explorer must stay standalone when no folder is opened: "No Folder Opened" view is missing `canMoveView`
body:
- VS Code Version: 1.136.2 (88e44fa0e00b08f7758b4f6d05632e4fd5e4df6f, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### Summary

With a folder open, the Explorer's **Folders** view (`workbench.explorer.fileView`) can be dragged into any other view container — e.g. into a Panel container shared with Terminal, Source Control and Search — and it stays there.

With **no folder open**, that is impossible. The Explorer container can be moved to the Panel as a whole, but it can only ever exist as a standalone container: its single view, **No Folder Opened** (`workbench.explorer.emptyView`), cannot be dragged at all, so it cannot be merged next to other views. Every other view in my layout can be.

The net effect is that a layout built with a folder open cannot be reproduced in an empty window, and the Explorer visually "jumps" out of the Panel back into its own container whenever the last folder is closed or a new empty window is opened.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a folder.
2. Drag **Explorer → Folders** onto the Panel, into the same container as Terminal / Source Control / Search. They sit side by side. ✔
3. Close the folder (or open a new empty window, <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd>).
4. The Explorer is now a standalone container again. Try to drag **No Folder Opened** into the container holding Terminal / Source Control / Search.

**Expected:** the view can be dropped there, like every other movable view.
**Actual:** the view is not draggable and no drop target is offered; the Explorer stays standalone.

### Root cause

`createEmptyViewDescriptor()` omits `canMoveView`, while its counterpart `createExplorerViewDescriptor()` sets `canMoveView: true`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0af2bfdddee61954b27fdb831f7a8b20a139126b/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/explorerViewlet.ts#L125-L152

`canMoveView` is optional and `undefined` is falsy, so both the drag source and the drop target reject the view in `viewPaneContainer.ts` (`if (viewDescriptor?.canMoveView)` at L1319, and `!viewDescriptor.canMoveView` in the drop handlers at L439 / L908).

The two descriptors are already inconsistent in the other direction (`canToggleVisibility` is `true` for the empty view and `false` for the folders view), which suggests the missing flag is an oversight rather than a deliberate restriction. Adding `canMoveView: true` to `createEmptyViewDescriptor()` looks like it would be enough.

title: Agent Host sandbox toggle uses client OS instead of remote host OS
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Reproduction

1. Use a macOS VS Code client connected to an Agent Host running on Windows.
2. Open a Copilot Agent Host session using the SDK built-in PowerShell tool.
3. Observe that the permissions UI does not indicate that sandboxing is enabled for the Windows host.
4. Run a PowerShell command that needs sandbox bypass.

## Actual behavior

The session prompts:

> Run in terminal outside the sandbox?

After approval, the tool fails with:

> GenericFailure: Sandboxing is enabled but not supported on this platform: Windows sandboxing requires BaseContainer. Update Windows to a supported version: https://aka.ms/ghcp-sandbox-os-support

This also happens with the session permission level set to **Allow all**, because sandbox bypass is intentionally treated as privilege elevation.

Agent Host logs show:

- the SDK sandbox configuration was applied via `session.options.update`
- `sdkMode=allow-all`
- the PowerShell request still required confirmation as a sandbox-bypass request
- managed settings contained `remoteControl,permissions`, with `failClosed=false`; sandboxing did not appear to be enforced by managed policy

## Expected behavior

The permissions picker should reflect the effective sandbox state of the target Agent Host. A macOS client connected to a Windows Agent Host should display and update the Windows sandbox setting used by that host.

If Windows sandbox support is unavailable, an experiment/default should not silently enable it and leave the session unable to execute terminal commands.

## Suspected cause

The client-side picker resolves the setting using the renderer's local platform:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentService.ts#L295-L297

`getAgentHostCopilotSandboxSettingId(..., windows = isWindows)` therefore selects the macOS/Linux setting on a macOS client, even when the connected Agent Host runs on Windows.

Meanwhile, `AgentHostSandboxForwarder` forwards all sandbox settings to every connected Agent Host, and the Windows host consumes `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/agentHostSandboxForwarder.ts

This allows the UI to read `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` while the target host executes with `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`. The Windows setting is also experiment-controlled with `mode: auto`, so it may be enabled without a deliberate user edit.

Session-specific sandbox settings added in #335364 make the effective target state especially important to surface accurately.

## Suggested fix

Derive the toggle from the target Agent Host platform and effective root/session sandbox configuration rather than the local renderer OS. Prefer having the Agent Host report its effective sandbox state so the picker cannot diverge from what is sent to the SDK.

It would also help to log the applied sandbox `enabled` state and target platform (without filesystem policy details) when calling `session.options.update`.

## Workaround

Explicitly set:

```json
"chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows": "off"
```

title: Automatic session cleanup can archive or delete using stale eligibility after a GitHub refresh
body:
Related test plan: [Test: Automatic cleanup settings for merged agent sessions (#335536)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335536)
Implementation: [#334341](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/334341)

## Summary and user impact

Automatic archival and permanent deletion share a check-before-await race: they validate the current cleanup settings/session eligibility, then await a final GitHub PR refresh, and act without rechecking the local facts afterward. Those facts can change while the request is pending.

Consequences include:

- **Permanent deletion after the user disables auto-delete**, even when the host has already received the setting change.
- **Automatic archival after the user starts a new turn or disables auto-archive.** Archival also starts worktree cleanup, which is inappropriate once the session is running. Existing Git safety checks still apply; this report does not demonstrate loss of uncommitted files.
- **A concurrent manual archive acquires automatic-archive provenance**, making that session eligible for later automatic deletion even though manually archived sessions should be exempt.

These are two paths with the same underlying cause, tracked here as one issue.

## Repro: permanent deletion

Use only disposable sessions/repositories. This operation is irreversible. The following is a controlled timing repro; hitting the overlap manually on a healthy connection would be difficult.

1. Have an internal, idle session with one merged related PR and no open related PRs. It must have been **automatically archived**, and its separate post-archive deletion grace period must have elapsed. Enable `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays` with a positive integer. Use a session with no remaining worktree to isolate the validation race.
2. Trigger a cleanup evaluation, for example by reloading the host. Using a local test responder/proxy or an asynchronous test barrier, hold the **final** PR refresh response after local eligibility has been checked. For a one-PR deletion candidate, this is the third `resolveForLifecycle` call in the evaluation. Do not pause the entire host: it must remain able to process configuration changes.
3. While that response is held, set `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays` to `0`. Wait until the change has reached the host, rather than merely changing the Settings UI.
4. Release the response with the PR still reported as merged.

**Expected:** The now-disabled operation is skipped and the session remains archived.

**Actual:** Final validation returns true and invokes permanent deletion using the setting check from before the wait.

## Repro: automatic archival

1. Have an internal, idle, unarchived session older than the configured inactivity threshold, with one merged related PR and no open related PRs. Enable `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays` with a positive integer.
2. Trigger evaluation and hold the final PR refresh response, as above. For a one-PR archive candidate, this is the second `resolveForLifecycle` call.
3. While the response is held, perform one of these changes and let the host apply it:
   - Set the archive setting to `0`;
   - Start a turn so the session becomes in progress; or
   - Manually archive the session.
4. Release the response with the PR still merged.

**Expected:** Skip automatic archival based on the changed setting/state; in particular, do not grant automatic-deletion eligibility to the m

In editor chat inputs backed by the shared `ChatInputPart`, the disabled **Send** action can receive keyboard focus and correctly exposes `aria-disabled="true"`, but it has no visible focus indicator. The focus-ring selector explicitly excludes `.disabled`, while the action label removes its native outline. This makes keyboard focus appear to skip or lose the Send button.

The Agents Window new-session composer is not affected because it uses the separate `Button` implementation and retains its disabled focus treatment.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an editor chat input with no sendable content.
2. Navigate by keyboard to the disabled Send button.
3. Observe that focus reaches the button, but no focus indicator is visible.

## Expected behavior

The disabled Send button shows the same circular focus indicator as the enabled Send button. It remains exposed as `aria-disabled` and Enter/Space or pointer activation remain no-ops.

## Affected surfaces

Shared `ChatInputPart` surfaces, including editor chat and other workbench/active-session chat inputs that use the same Send action styling. The Agents Window new-session composer is excluded.

title: Dev Container sessions: Configure Git safe.directory
body:
Dev Container Agent Host sessions can encounter Git's "detected dubious ownership" error when the repository is bind-mounted from the host and owned by a different user inside the container.

The fix detects the exact repository root, maps it through its Docker bind mount, verifies that the corresponding host directory is owned by the current host user, and then adds only that repository root to the container user's global `safe.directory` list.

Original fix: #335717

1.138 cherry-pick: #336047

## Setup

- Enable **Chat: Remote Agent Hosts Enabled** and **Chat › Agent Host › Dev Container: Enabled**.
- If Docker is not installed, install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), then start Docker.
- Fork, then clone the [Node.js Dev Container sample](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node).
- Open the Agents Window.

## Test

1. Start a new session and open the workspace picker.
2. Open the local folder submenu for the cloned sample and choose **Use Dev Container**.
4. Ask the agent to run `git status` in the repository.
3. Wait for the Dev Container Agent Host connection to complete.
5. Verify Git succeeds without a "detected dubious ownership" error.
6. Ask the agent to run (or run in the integrated terminal yourself) `git config --global --get-all safe.directory`.
7. Verify the output contains the exact repository root inside the container, rather than only the workspace mount root.
8. Open the **Output** view, select the **Dev Container (\<folder\>)** channel, and verify it reports the `safe.directory` configuration duration without unexpected errors.

title: Copilot managed OTel policy can be missed during extension activation
body:
## Summary

Enterprise-managed Copilot OpenTelemetry settings can be missed during VS Code startup. The configuration model eventually reports the managed values correctly, but the already-running Copilot extension can remain on its startup fallback for the lifetime of that extension host and export no enterprise telemetry.

The outcome is nondeterministic and is easier to reproduce when many windows are restored concurrently or when managed-settings resolution is delayed.

## Managed configuration

For example:

```json
{
  "telemetry": {
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint": "https://collector.example.com",
    "protocol": "http/json",
    "captureContent": true,
    "lockCaptureContent": true,
    "serviceName": "github-copilot"
  }
}
```

## Observed behavior

A successful activation logs both the extension exporter and the embedded Copilot runtime exporter:

```text
[OTel] Instrumentation enabled — exporter=otlp-http endpoint=https://collector.example.com/ captureContent=true
[CopilotCLI] OpenTelemetry enabled: exporter=otlp-http, source=github.copilot
```

A failed activation logs only:

```text
[CopilotCLI] OpenTelemetry enabled: exporter=file, source=github.copilot
```

There is no warning or OTLP connection attempt. Later, **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** reports the managed OTel values as successfully applied even though that extension host is still not exporting to the managed endpoint.

Restarting only the extension host after policy has resolved generally makes the next activation use the managed exporter.

## Root cause

Two startup paths are not ordered.

### Late policy-reference registration

`PolicyConfiguration.initialize()` resolves keys registered at initial configuration startup. Extension-contributed settings are registered later. Their policy references are processed by an async listener in:

`src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configurations.ts`

```ts
this._register(this.defaultConfiguration.onDidChangeConfiguration(
  async ({ properties }) => this.update(await this.updatePolicyDefinitions(properties), true)));
```

The event source does not await the listener's promise before extension activation continues.

### One-shot OTel service construction

Copilot resolves its OTel configuration once during service registration in:

`extensions/copilot/src/extension/extension/vscode-node/services.ts`

```ts
const otelSettings = workspace.getConfiguration('github.copilot.chat.otel');
const policyValue = key => otelSettings.inspect(key)?.policyValue;
const otelConfig = resolveOTelConfig(/* ... */);
```

It then permanently registers either `NodeOTelService` or `InMemoryOTelService` for that extension-host activation.

If the late policy references have not resolved yet, all `policyValue` reads are `undefined`. The service is constructed without enterprise OTel enabled. When policy arrives later, the VS Code configuration model updates, but the OTel service is not recreated or reconfigured.

The reload watcher in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/otel/vscode-node/otelContrib.ts` does not reliably recover this case. It is registered after service construction and snapshots the then-current values. Policy can resolve after the service read but before the watcher snapshot, leaving the service stale without a later change to trigger a reload prompt.

## Why `exporter=file` appears

This is the expected fallback in:

`extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/node/copilotcliSessionService.ts`

When the frozen

title: Dev Container setup failures do not reveal detailed diagnostics
body:
Refs #335766

When starting an Agent Host session in a Dev Container fails, the relevant Output channel is not automatically revealed and the Dev Container CLI output does not contain enough detail to diagnose the failure.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable **Chat: Remote Agent Hosts Enabled** and **Chat › Agent Host › Dev Container: Enabled**.
2. If Docker is not installed, install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/).
3. Make sure Docker is not running.
4. Fork, then clone the [Node.js Dev Container sample](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-try-node).
5. Open the Agents Window.
6. Start a new session, select the cloned folder, and choose **Use Dev Container**.

## Actual behavior

Dev Container setup fails, but the workspace-specific Dev Container Output channel is not revealed automatically and its default logging does not provide enough diagnostic detail.

## Expected behavior

The **Output** view should automatically reveal the **Dev Container (<folder>)** channel when setup fails. The channel should contain debug-level Dev Container CLI and Docker output while the original setup error is still reported to the user. Canceling setup should not reveal the channel.

## Steps to verify

1. Use a build containing https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/336119 and make sure Docker is not running.
2. Start a new session, select the cloned folder, and choose **Use Dev Container**.
3. Verify setup fails and the **Output** view is automatically revealed with the **Dev Container (\<folder\>)** channel selected.
4. Verify the channel contains debug-level Dev Container CLI diagnostics that identify Docker as unavailable.
5. Verify the original setup error is still reported to the user.
6. Start Docker and retry; verify the Dev Container Agent Host session starts successfully.
7. Start another Dev Container session and cancel setup; verify cancellation does not reveal the Output channel.

title: Feature: Support extraBody configuration for BYOK custom models
body:
## Summary

Allow BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) custom models to configure additional request body fields via an `extraBody` property in `chatLanguageModels.json`. This would enable users to pass model-specific parameters that are not currently supported through the existing `modelOptions` configuration.
(**This text was created with Copilot!**)

## Use Case

When using custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (like vLLM, local inference servers, or specialized APIs), models often require additional parameters beyond the currently supported `temperature` and `top_p`:

- `reasoning_effort` (for reasoning models)
- `preserve_thinking` (to retain internal reasoning in responses)
- `chat_template_kwargs` (for custom chat template configuration)
- Provider-specific parameters for cache control, routing, or session management
- Custom model options (e.g., `output_config`, nested configuration objects)

### Example Configuration

```json
{
  "vendor": "customendpoint",
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",
      "name": "2xDGX-GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",
      "url": "http://myAIServer:8600/v1",
      "toolCalling": true,
      "vision": true,
      "maxInputTokens": 262144,
      "maxOutputTokens": 32768,
      "modelOptions": {
        "temperature": 0.2,
        "top_p": 0.95
      },
      "extraBody": {
        "reasoning_effort": "none",
        "preserve_thinking": false,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "enable_thinking": false
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Current Limitations

1. **Only `temperature` and `top_p` are supported** in `modelOptions` (see `byokProvider.ts` lines 308-321 and `openAIEndpoint.ts` lines 302-324)
2. **No generic body customization** - users cannot pass arbitrary request body fields
3. **Model initialization failures** - models that require additional parameters cannot be properly configured
4. **Inconsistent with other extensions** - some extensions (e.g., Kilo Code) already support custom header and body configuration

## Proposed Solution

### Option A: Flexible `extraBody` Field (Recommended)

Add an optional `extraBody` field to model capabilities that allows arbitrary JSON to be merged into the request body:

```typescript
export interface BYOKModelCapabilities {
  // ... existing fields ...
  /**
   * Additional fields to merge into the request body.
   * These override default values but can be overridden by per-request parameters.
   */
  extraBody?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

**Implementation:**
- Merge `extraBody` into the request body after model options are applied
- Deep merge for nested objects
- Per-request parameters take precedence

### Option B: Explicit Parameter List

Extend `modelOptions` to support common additional parameters:
- `reasoning_effort`
- `preserve_thinking`
- Custom output configuration options

**Pros:** More type-safe, better validation
**Cons:** Less flexible, requires updating schema for each new parameter

## Additional Context

- Related to #316794 (custom headers request)
- Affects users of local deployments (vLLM, ollama, custom inference servers)
- Impacts compatibility with specialized reasoning models (DeepSeek, Claude with thinking)
- See #312746 for related issue with reasoning content handling

## Suggested Implementation Path

1. Add `extraBody?: Record<string, unknown>` to `BYOKModelCapabilities` interface
2. Update JSON schema in `package.json` to allow `extraBody` object
3. Modify `OpenAIEndpoint._applyConfiguredModelOptions()` to merge

title: Agent host logs an error when releasing sampling interest during shutdown
body:
## Problem

When an agent-host session shuts down, cleanup can try to release the MCP sampling interest after the SDK session has already gone away. This produces an error during an otherwise normal shutdown.

Example:

```text
[trace] [Copilot:<session-id>] Session shutdown: type=routine, apiDuration=0ms
[error] Error: Request session.eventLog.releaseInterest failed with message: Session not found for sessionId: <session-id>
[Copilot:<session-id>] Failed to release sampling event interest
```

The sampling interest should be released before disconnecting the SDK session. If the session has already shut down, there is nothing left to release.

title: MCP HTTP client: cross-origin redirect handling strips credentials from the caller's headers, so a retry to the original server goes out without Mcp-Session-Id and Cookie
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: main (f44f55cde0c), also present in current Insiders
- OS Version: Linux x64 (Pop!_OS 22.04)

Since #320347, `McpHTTPHandle._fetch` removes `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Proxy-Authorization` and `Mcp-Session-Id` when a redirect crosses origins. It does so with `delete init.headers[name]` on the `init` object it received, and that object belongs to the caller: `_sendStreamableHttp`, `_attachStreamableBackchannel` and `_attachSSE` pass the same `headers` object both as `init.headers` and as the `headers` argument of `_fetchWithAuthRetry`, whose retry is `() => this._fetch(mcpUrl, init)`.

After one cross-origin hop, a retry against the configured server (for example after a 401 from the redirect target) is therefore sent to the original origin without `Mcp-Session-Id` and `Cookie`. `Authorization` is put back by `_addAuthHeader`; the other two are not. For a streamable-HTTP server the retry arrives without the session id, which the server may reject as an unknown session.

Steps to Reproduce (unit level):

1. Call `_fetch` with `headers = { 'Mcp-Session-Id': 's', Cookie: 'a=b', Authorization: 'Bearer t' }` against a server that answers 307 to another origin.
2. After the call returns, inspect the `headers` object that was passed in: `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Cookie` and `Authorization` are gone.
3. Call `_fetch` again with the same `init` against the original origin: the request goes out without them.

Expected: the stripping applies to the redirected request only, as `fetch` does in browsers, and the caller's headers are left intact.

title: Codex Agent Host Auto-Review approves sandbox escalation but still runs the command inside the sandbox on macOS
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.138.0
- Commit: 7debcd0e2acdea1c52de81bf9ee1620444407dda
- OS: macOS arm64
- Codex Agent Host bundled SDK: 0.153.0
- Session target: Codex on Agent Host
- Permission preset: Auto-Review

## Description

When Codex runs through the experimental Agent Host, Auto-Review accepts an explicit sandbox escalation request, but the command is still executed under the same managed sandbox profile.

This makes Auto-Review unusable for routine commands that need read access outside the workspace, including Git reading the user configuration and Apple developer tools reading or updating their caches.

The same commands work immediately after selecting Full Access. They also worked through the OpenAI Codex extension before switching to Agent Host.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled`.
2. Enable `chat.editor.codex.preferAgentHost` and restart VS Code.
3. Start a local Codex Agent Host session in a Git repository on macOS.
4. Select the Auto-Review permission preset.
5. Run `git status --short` through the Codex shell tool.
6. Observe the sandbox failure.
7. Retry the command with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"` and a justification.
8. Auto-Review does not reject the request, but the retry produces the same sandbox errors.
9. Select Full Access and run the same command. It succeeds immediately.

## Actual behavior

The initial command fails with errors similar to:

```text
git: error: could not create cache file /var/folders/.../T/xcrun_db-* (errno=Operation not permitted)
fatal: unable to access $HOME/.gitconfig: Operation not permitted
```

Reading an explicitly configured user skill outside the workspace behaves the same way:

```text
sed: $HOME/.agents/skills/example/SKILL.md: Operation not permitted
```

An explicit `require_escalated` retry accepted by Auto-Review returns the same errors, which indicates that the sandbox override is ignored or lost between the reviewer decision and command execution.

## Expected behavior

After Auto-Review approves `require_escalated`, VS Code should rerun the command outside the managed sandbox, matching the documented escalation behavior.

If the automatic reviewer cannot authorize an unsandboxed retry, VS Code should surface a human approval prompt instead of silently rerunning with unchanged restrictions.

## Additional information

- Full Access proves that the binaries, files, and commands themselves are valid.
- Default Permissions and Auto-Review use the same workspace access, but Auto-Review routes approval requests to the automatic reviewer.
- Codex Agent Host currently overrides custom Codex permission configuration, so `~/.codex/config.toml` cannot provide a narrower workaround.

Possibly related:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333898
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334445
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36391

title: Long-running Agent Host sessions accumulate issue and pull-request references without cleanup
body:
## Description

In a long-running Agent Host session in the Agents Window, the resource pills beside the chat input keep accumulating every recorded GitHub issue and pull request. Older entries remain indefinitely, and there is no visible way to remove individual stale references or clear a collection.

In the observed session, the input footer had grown to:

- 15 Pull Requests
- 15 Issues
- 2 Artifacts

As the session continues, these collections become increasingly noisy and make it difficult to find the resources that are relevant to the current work.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host session in the Agents Window.
2. Keep using the same session across multiple tasks involving GitHub issues and pull requests.
3. Record or encounter additional issues and pull requests throughout the session.
4. Observe the resource pills beside the chat input.

## Actual behavior

- Issue and pull-request entries continually accumulate for the lifetime of the session.
- Old or no-longer-relevant references remain mixed with current ones.
- The UI offers no apparent way to remove an individual entry or clear stale references.
- The summary counts continue growing, making the collections less useful over time.

## Expected behavior

Long-running sessions should have a manageable lifecycle for recorded resources. The UI should remain useful as references accumulate, for example by allowing stale entries to be removed or cleared and by avoiding duplicate entries for the same resource.

Explicitly recorded durable artifacts can remain persistent if that is intentional, but ordinary issue and pull-request references should not grow without any user control.

## Related work

- #335383 addressed preserving issue and pull-request titles in these pills.
- #335896 covers rich previews and interaction with the collections.

This report is specifically about retention and unbounded collection growth rather than pill rendering or preview content.

title: On-device dictation reports empty finalization timeouts as completed
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested; reproduced with controlled dependencies executing the source methods.

- VS Code Version: Eight-second fallback verified in 1.137.0 and 1.138.0 source; reproduction at `4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d`.
- OS Version: Windows; source-method reproduction, not a real-microphone test.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start local dictation with no transcript available and keep backend preparation/finalization pending in a test fixture.
2. Stop dictation and allow the eight-second finalization deadline to expire.

**Actual:** The backend is cancelled, no text is returned, and session telemetry records `completed`, `errorCode=""`, and `transcriptLength=0`.

**Expected:** Distinguish an empty timeout fallback from successful completion, while preserving the deadline and any useful partial transcript.

### Potential root cause
`_finishBackend()` warns on timeout and returns the streamed transcript without setting a timeout outcome. `_stopAndTranscribe()` therefore records `completed` even when the fallback is empty. Native `stop()` waits for model preparation too, so stopping before the model is ready can take this path.

Sources: [timeout fallback](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1540-L1557), [completion reporting](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1350-L1361).

A controlled reproduction exercised the actual eight-second deadline. This explains the empty timeout outcome, not why each affected session produced no transcript.

title: On-device dictation can ignore model startup errors and report an empty completion
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested; reproduced with controlled dependencies executing the source methods.

- VS Code Version: Startup gap verified in 1.137.0 and 1.138.0 source; reproduction at `4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d`.
- OS Version: Windows; source-method reproduction, not a real-microphone test.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start local dictation with a test backend that fails immediately and returns model status `Error` from `getModelStatus()`.
2. Stop dictation after the renderer enters Recording.

**Actual:** No startup failure is surfaced; stop returns no text and records `completed` with `transcriptLength=0`.

**Expected:** Surface the startup error and terminate the session as failed.

### Potential root cause
`_startLocalSession()` skips status tracking when the initial snapshot is already `Error`. `_failSession()` also ignores failures while the renderer is still Idle during startup. Native `stop()` then catches the failed-open promise and returns empty text, assuming the error was already handled.

Sources: [renderer startup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1045-L1078), [startup failure guard](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1250-L1265), [native stop](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4fa9fcf245ad90eb1f21fae5ed0511515e068b1d/src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts#L715-L743).

The combined startup/stop path was reproduced with synthetic dependencies; its production frequency is not established.

title: Voice Mode: record a categorized rejection reason for invalid confirmation narrations
body:
### Problem

When the voice backend rejects a confirmation narration with a `narration_ack` disposition of `invalid`, the client drops the narration and emits `voiceNarrationDropped` with `kind: 'confirmation'` and `reason: 'invalid'`. This identifies the outcome, but not why the backend rejected the request, making it difficult to diagnose confirmations that are not spoken.

`IVoiceNarrationAck` already includes an optional backend `reason`. `_handleNarrationAck` writes it to the local trace log but does not include a diagnostic category in telemetry.

### Proposed change

Preserve the existing `reason` field as the disposition/drop category, and add a separate bounded, categorized rejection-reason field to `voiceNarrationDropped` for invalid confirmation narrations.

- Define an allowlisted set of stable reason codes based on the backend contract. Coordinate a typed backend reason code if the current reason is free-form.
- Map missing or unrecognized reasons to explicit `missing`/`unknown` categories.
- Do not forward raw backend reason text, narration text, transcripts, session descriptions, or identifiers into the new field.
- Add the appropriate telemetry classification and document the new field's semantics.
- Preserve existing narration drop/retry behavior.

### Relevant code

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/voiceClient/voiceClientService.ts`: `IVoiceNarrationAck.reason`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceSessionController.ts`: `_handleNarrationAck`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceTelemetry.ts`: `VoiceNarrationDroppedEvent` and `VoiceNarrationDroppedClassification`

### Acceptance criteria

- Invalid confirmation narration events distinguish known rejection causes while retaining `kind: 'confirmation'` and `reason: 'invalid'`.
- Missing/unrecognized backend reasons do not leak free-form content.
- Focused tests cover known, missing, and unrecognized reasons, and verify that accepted/busy acknowledgements retain their existing behavior.

cc @meganrogge

title: MCP Registry remote URL variables are not converted during install
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Description

VS Code accepts MCP Registry manifests using the `2025-12-11` `server.json` schema, but does not convert variables declared on a remote transport when generating `mcp.json`.

The schema permits remote URLs such as:

```json
{
  "type": "streamable-http",
  "url": "https://{environment_id}.example.com/mcp",
  "variables": {
    "environment_id": {
      "description": "Environment ID",
      "isRequired": true,
      "format": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

VS Code processes variables declared in headers and arguments, but copies `remotes[].url` unchanged and drops `remotes[].variables`. The installed server consequently has an unresolved hostname and no input through which the user can provide the environment ID.

This affects multi-tenant remote MCP servers whose tenant, environment, region, or deployment identifier forms part of the endpoint URL. The [Dynatrace MCP server manifest](https://github.com/Dynatrace/dynatrace-for-ai/blob/main/server.json) is one concrete example.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a `server.json` manifest with the `2025-12-11` schema and a `remotes[]` entry containing a URL placeholder plus a matching `variables` declaration.
2. Run **MCP: Install Server from Manifest...** and select the manifest, or install the same entry from an MCP Registry.
3. Run **MCP: Open User Configuration**.
4. Inspect the generated server URL and top-level `inputs` array.

## Actual behavior

The generated configuration keeps the Registry placeholder literal:

```jsonc
"url": "https://{environment_id}.example.com/mcp"
```

No `environment_id` entry is added to `inputs`. Starting the server therefore uses an unresolved/literal hostname rather than prompting the user.

## Expected behavior

VS Code should convert declared Registry URL placeholders into its configuration-input syntax:

```jsonc
"url": "https://${input:environment_id}.example.com/mcp"
```

It should also create the corresponding top-level input using the description, secret flag, default, and choices from the Registry declaration. Explicit fixed values should be substituted directly rather than exposed as prompts.

## Schema references

- Published [`2025-12-11` JSON Schema](https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json)
- [`RemoteTransport.variables`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml#L900-L912)
- [`ServerDetail.remotes[]` references `RemoteTransport`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml#L999-L1002)
- Feature introduction: [modelcontextprotocol/registry#570](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/pull/570)
- Schema release: [modelcontextprotocol/registry#841](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/pull/841)

## Additional considerations

- Support both streamable HTTP and SSE remotes.
- Replace repeated occurrences of a declared placeholder while leaving undeclared placeholders unchanged.
- Deduplicate compatible variables shared between URLs and headers.
- Do not silently discard conflicting defaults, choices, or secret metadata for the same input ID.
- Preserve registry-only access checks by treating the Registry and generated VS Code template forms as equivalent, without introducing wildcard URL matching.

title: Remote session reopen can show a stale, incomplete conversation
Allow agents to create research sessions without a new worktree
body:
When an orchestrating agent creates a session for read-only research, the session is still created with a new worktree even when the agent omits the `worktree` option. This is surprising because the agent interprets omission as opting out of worktree creation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ask an agent to create a child/session for a read-only research task.
2. Have the agent omit the `worktree` option because no code changes are expected.
3. Observe that the session is created in a new worktree anyway.

## Expected behavior

The session creation API should provide a clear, explicit way for an orchestrating agent to create a session in the current workspace without allocating a new worktree. The tool schema/documentation should also make the default behavior unambiguous so agents do not assume omission disables worktree creation.

## Actual behavior

Omitting `worktree` still creates a new worktree, causing unnecessary worktrees for research-only questions.

title: Agents Window session status stays stale after continuing from another client
body:
## Type of issue
Bug

## Description

When a previously opened multi-chat Agent Host session is continued from another client/device, its row in the Agents Window can remain in its old state until the session is opened or focused locally.

The Agent Host publishes the status transition and VS Code receives it, but the row continues rendering stale cached per-chat state rather than the updated aggregate session status.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a multi-chat/subagent session in the Agents Window so its per-chat catalog is hydrated.
2. Navigate away and allow its live session-state subscription to be released.
3. Leave the session waiting or completed.
4. Continue the main chat from another client/device.
5. Observe the session row in VS Code without opening it.

## Expected

The row immediately changes to **In Progress** when the root session summary reports `InProgress`.

## Actual

The aggregate `ISession.status` changes, but the row continues displaying the stale cached main-chat status. Opening/focusing the session starts a full session subscription, refreshes per-chat status, and makes the row correct itself.

## Debug-log evidence

Observed in VS Code Insiders on 2026-09-20. The full debug bundle is available privately but is not attached because it contains sensitive session data.

- `14:02:10`: `listSessions` reports protocol status `56` (`InputNeeded | IsRead`).
- `14:02:41.034`: Agent Host sends `root/sessionSummaryChanged` with status `40` (`InProgress | IsRead`).
- `14:02:41.035`: the renderer receives the notification.
- `14:02:41.096`: session management reports `onDidChangeSessions` with one changed session.
- There is no full subscription to this session during the background period, so no fresh per-chat statuses reach VS Code.
- `14:05:56.474`: opening/focusing the session subscribes to its full state.
- `14:05:56.636`: the snapshot reports aggregate status `40`, default-chat status `8` (`InProgress`), and three running tool-origin chats. The visible row then corrects itself.

This rules out a missed Agent Host notification or transport failure: the authoritative aggregate status reached the renderer before focus.

## Likely cause

The Agent Host provider's `root/sessionSummaryChanged` handler updates only `cached.status`:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a24c5eb8ae975a0ab61822673fa0702db1335f60/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L6405-L6430

For a hydrated multi-chat session, the main chat prefers `_defaultChatStatusOverride` over aggregate session status:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a24c5eb8ae975a0ab61822673fa0702db1335f60/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L1181

That override is refreshed from the full chat catalog:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a24c5eb8ae975a0ab61822673fa0702db1335f60/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L1300-L1320

Full session state is pinned only for sessions visible/open in the Agents grid, not every sidebar row:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a24c5eb8ae975a0ab61822673fa0702db1335f60/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L5484-L5519

Meanwhile, the main Sessions list enables `deriveStatusFromMainChat` and its row-status helper returns cached main/child chat status instead of the aggregate status:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a24c5eb8ae975a0

title: Server-managed private plugin marketplace cannot use VS Code session credentials
body:
## Summary

A private GitHub plugin marketplace configured through **server-delivered Copilot managed settings** (`extraKnownMarketplaces`) is not usable from VS Code, even though the managed setting is delivered. If the user manually adds the same marketplace, VS Code asks for GitHub/Git credentials and the marketplace then works.

This issue is specifically about the server-delivered channel. It is distinct from the native-MDM object parsing issue in #333816.

cc @pwang347

## Reproduction

1. Configure an enterprise AI controls source organization.
2. In the source organization's `.github-private/copilot/managed-settings.json`, configure a private GitHub marketplace:

   ```json
   {
     "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
       "acme-private": {
         "source": {
           "source": "github",
           "repo": "acme/private-agent-plugins"
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   Optionally enable a plugin from that marketplace through `enabledPlugins`.
3. Sign in to GitHub Copilot in VS Code, with the usable GitHub credential held by the editor/Agent Host session rather than a separate persisted Copilot CLI login or preconfigured system Git credential.
4. Run **Developer: Sync Account Policy** or restart VS Code.
5. Confirm in **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** that `extraKnownMarketplaces` was delivered.
6. Open the Agent Plugins marketplace/catalog.

## Actual behavior

The managed marketplace is unavailable or yields no plugins. The managed configuration does not cause an actionable GitHub authentication flow.

If the same `owner/repo` marketplace is then added manually, the operation reaches Git authentication, asks the user to authenticate, and succeeds. This creates a per-user configuration entry for a marketplace that enterprise policy was intended to provide automatically.

## Expected behavior

A private GitHub marketplace supplied by server-managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` should be registered and accessed using the active VS Code/Agent Host authentication context, or should present a deterministic sign-in/retry action. Users should not need to duplicate the managed marketplace in user settings.

Authentication/access failures should identify the affected marketplace and remain visible instead of degrading to an empty marketplace result.

## Findings

The server-managed policy projection itself is working:

- `normalizeExtraKnownMarketplaces` converts the server response into the canonical policy value.
- `readConfiguredMarketplaces` unions `chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces` with user-configured marketplaces.
- Agent Host sessions opt into managed-settings resolution with `enableManagedSettings: true`.

The remaining gap is the authentication context used for marketplace operations:

- VS Code's desktop marketplace path first probes anonymous `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs and then falls back to a local `git clone`.
- The native clone path invokes local Git without receiving the active Agent Host session's GitHub credential.
- Background marketplace discovery can reduce a clone/access failure to an empty result; the explicit refresh command has better per-marketplace error reporting.
- Manual addition/install reaches the interactive clone/credential path, which explains why it can prompt and then work.

Upstream has the same authentication-context split for standalone marketplace commands in github/copilot-cli#4556. github/copilot-agent-runtime#21105 shipped in runtime/CLI 1.0.87 and fixed environment, `gh`, broker, and pe

title: Bound Linux smoke-test disk diagnostics to avoid job timeout
body:
## Summary

The Linux Electron Tests job in build [475743](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=475743&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=c6def06e-f043-549c-e923-f5085dee008a) hit its 50-minute timeout after the pre-smoke diagnostic spent 12m40s running `du -xhd1 /`.

All unit, integration, and smoke tests completed successfully. The later Component Governance task was canceled only because the diagnostic consumed the remaining job budget.

## Evidence

First attempt on `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64 23`:

- `Diagnostics before smoke test run`: 23:01:42–23:14:22 (**12m40s**)
- `Run smoke tests (Electron)`: succeeded in 10m52s
- `Component Governance`: started with ~19 seconds left and was canceled by the job timeout

Successful retry on `1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64 3`:

- Same diagnostic: **43s**
- Component Governance: succeeded in 42s
- Overall Linux stage and build succeeded

The long interval is visible directly around:

```text
23:01:42  --- top consumers on / ---
23:14:21  60G /
```

## Source

The root traversal was added in #322903 / commit 24cb1a383384:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/azure-pipelines/linux/steps/product-build-linux-test.yml

```bash
du -xhd1 / 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -30 || true
```

The step has `continueOnError: true`, but no task or command timeout. A successful but slow `du` therefore consumes the job timeout budget.

## Suggested fix

Preserve the disk-space diagnostics, but bound expensive traversals—for example with `timeout 60s du ...` (and similarly bound the other `du`/`lsof` diagnostics), or add a short task-level timeout. Diagnostic collection should not be able to prevent test/post-test work from completing.

title: Agent Host: reused background subagent approval is orphaned after parent cancellation, leaving chat at Analyzing
body:
# Agent Host: reusing background subagents after cancellation can orphan approval requests and leave chat at "Analyzing"

## Summary

A Copilot SDK chat remains active at **"Analyzing"**, with a Stop button but no approval UI. A background subagent is actually waiting for explicit shell approval.

Live debugging with the global `dbgjs` CLI confirmed that the SDK still knows the child and has its unresolved permission, but Agent Host no longer has the child's chat-routing registration. Child events, including the permission request, accumulate in `_pendingSubagentSignals` instead of reaching the client.

The affected session had earlier parent cancellations followed by reuse of the same background agents through `write_agent`. Cancellation deletes the child registrations, while subsequent SDK activity emits `subagent_resumed`, not a new `subagent_started`. The host rejects that resume as unknown, then buffers subsequent events indefinitely.

This is a lifecycle/routing problem, not a slow model request or merely a collapsed approval card.

## Environment

- Windows; VS Code **1.139.0-insider**.
- Installed build: `b040d43fe0c41719eabee1d41d3c16bb1c04a931`.
- Agent Host with the Copilot SDK backend.
- Parent model: GPT-6 Astra; affected background child: `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- Interactive session using Assisted permissions.
- A long-lived conversation, with background agents reused across multiple turns and parent cancellations.
- Session title: **Cover BugIndicatingError workers**.
- No isolated fresh-session reproduction was performed; the evidence below is from the actual stalled session.

## Expected behavior

Reusing a background agent after cancelling a parent turn should preserve or reconstruct its protocol chat and start a valid child turn. An explicit permission request should reach the normal approval UI and settle when the user approves or rejects it.

If the child cannot be resumed, it should fail visibly and settle outstanding requests. It must not continue generating events into an indefinitely pending buffer while the parent displays "Analyzing".

## Actual behavior and timeline

All times below are **September 22, 2026, local time UTC+02:00**. AHP and SDK event timestamps were converted from UTC.

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 18:47:48 | `team-tools-breakpoint-sol` starts as a background `general-purpose` agent. |
| 18:53:09 | Its initial run emits `subagent.completed`. Later work reuses the same agent. |
| 19:07:01 and 19:08:35 | Parent `chat/turnCancelled` actions occur. |
| 19:10:04 | Host logs `Cannot resume unknown subagent` for this child. |
| 19:21:22, 19:27:52, 20:00:22 | The same unknown-child resume error recurs. |
| 19:31:59, 20:29:36, 20:32:45 | Additional parent cancellation actions occur. |
| 20:44:09 | Another reused child also produces `Cannot resume unknown subagent`. |
| 20:47:50 | The currently displayed parent turn starts. |
| 20:56:40 and 20:59:00 | The packaging child's resume again fails as unknown. |
| 20:59:19 | Parent says it is waiting for background fixes/tests before reload and end-to-end retesting. |
| 21:07:29 | Packaging child starts a `powershell` tool request to package Windows npm artifacts. |
| 21:07:30 | Explicit permission is requested; no permission completion follows for this tool. |
| Approximately 21:12-21:19 | Screenshot, DOM, logs, heap snapshot, and live object inspection confirm the invisible outstanding approval and missing routing registration. |

The blocked command is:

title: Fix and re-enable flaky Windows Agent Host descendant cleanup test
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A — repository CI test failure, not an interactive extension scenario.

- VS Code Version: Source commit `13ac8f9c` in the reported Flaky Smoke Tests run `20260923.2`.
- OS Version: Windows CI; exact Windows version was not included in the available report.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On Windows, use the test at the reported revision, or locally restore its Windows-only registration if working from the quarantine change in #337629.
2. Repeatedly run `Agent Host test server cleanup > stops owned descendants after the server exits gracefully` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/serverIntegrationTestHelpers.test.ts`.

The available report records **1 failure / 20 executed runs** in Flaky Smoke Tests `20260923.2` at `13ac8f9c`. During descendant cleanup, `taskkill` intermittently exited with **code 255** and a **critical-system-process error**. This is intermittent; a single execution may pass. No build URL was available in the report, and this issue does not claim a fresh local reproduction.

### Expected behavior

The test reliably verifies that owned descendants are stopped after the server exits gracefully, without intermittent cleanup failures.

### Quarantine and ownership

#337629 changes only this test to `test.skip` and removes its unused `isWindows` import. It was already skipped on non-Windows platforms. The PR changes no production or process-cleanup behavior and is open, not yet merged, as of filing.

@chrmarti authored the test in #337080 ([introducing commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/bf715befd589605be045505d0456e4246054566f)). Assigning this follow-up to the test author to investigate, fix the flakiness, and re-enable its Windows coverage once reliable. Preserve the existing non-Windows skip unless platform coverage is deliberately expanded separately.

### Scope and uncertainty

- PID reuse was suggested in the report but is an **unconfirmed hypothesis**, not an established root cause.
- The separate integration `beforeEach` cleanup failures from the report are not addressed by this quarantine.
- The `ChatPetWidget` animation assertion failures observed in #337629's CI are unrelated to this follow-up.

### Completion criteria

Identify and address the cause of this test's intermittent Windows failure, demonstrate reliable repeated Windows runs, and remove the quarantine while restoring its intended Windows-only execution.

title: Combined permission and mode picker loses its background in dark themes
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Description

When a chat background is configured in the new Agents window chat, the combined **Mode + Permissions** picker has no opaque control background in a dark theme. The other controls in the same row retain their secondary-control backgrounds. The combined picker does have a visible background in a light theme.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the new Agents window chat.
2. Configure a chat background.
3. Use a dark color theme.
4. Compare the combined Mode + Permissions picker with the other controls in the composer row.
5. Switch to a light theme and compare again.

## Expected

The combined picker uses the same opaque secondary-control surface as the other composer controls in both light and dark themes.

## Actual

The combined picker appears transparent in dark themes, allowing the configured chat background to show through. It appears correctly surfaced in light themes.

## Investigation

The combined trigger is styled separately from the standard composer controls. `agentHostModePicker.css` explicitly gives `.agent-host-mode-permissions-trigger` a `background: transparent`, while the chat-background surface is restored through special-case selectors in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/media/chatView.css` and `chatWidget.css`. Ordinary controls do not depend on this split trigger override. The dark-theme failure appears to be a cascade/surface regression in that special path; the combined trigger should retain the same `button.secondaryBackground`-based opaque surface as its siblings, with the individual mode/permission segments only supplying hover/open-state overlays.

title: Support trusted “Try This” experiences in release notes and documentation
Managed settings are dropped after transient refresh failures
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded
- VS Code Version: Regression introduced by #330896; fixed on main by #337583 and backported to release/1.139 by #337739
- OS Version: Not recorded
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Enterprise managed settings / Copilot OpenTelemetry configuration
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A
- Logs: Not attached; diagnosis and validation are documented in #337583.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Sign in with an enterprise account that supplies server-managed settings, such as an OpenTelemetry endpoint, and allow a successful settings fetch.
2. Allow the cached response to become older than one hour, then encounter a failed refresh (no response, transient 401/403, 429, 5xx, or malformed response).
3. Observe that the previously applied policy is dropped. A subsequent successful fetch restores it.

**Actual behavior:** Managed settings alternate between the enterprise policy and defaults during refresh failures. For an OTel endpoint, affected users see recurring notifications such as "Copilot OTel endpoint will change to http://localhost:4318 after reload.", especially after idle. Other server-managed restrictions are also temporarily lifted.

**Expected behavior:** A failed refresh is not evidence that policy was withdrawn. Keep the last successful settings, even when stale, without renewing their original fetch timestamp so subsequent polls or focus events retry. Successful responses, explicit withdrawal, sign-out/account changes, and forced-refresh behavior retain their existing semantics.

**Fix and release tracking**

- Main fix: #337583 (merged).
- Cherry-pick: #337739 (merged into `release/1.139`).

This issue tracks the stale-policy retention regression addressed by those PRs. The separate session-lookup-error and `managedSettingsActive` lifecycle problems described in #337583 are outside this issue's scope.

title: SDK hangs due to spamming listSessions
body:
A couple times a day, the SDK uses 800% CPU for awhile and AH sessions hang. Seems that refreshing sessions is misbehaving somehow. Can provide logs

```
Yes. The logs provide a strong smoking gun, and it is **not primarily thousands of `getSessionMetadata` calls**.

## What happened

### 1. Repeated bulk `listSessions` prewarming

`agenthost.log` recorded:

- **111** “Listing prewarm session metadata” passes
- Each pass enumerated approximately **4,854–4,858 SDK sessions**
- Total session records enumerated: **538,958**
- Median pass: **1.42 seconds**
- Slowest pass: **84.4 seconds**
- Since 16:50, four passes enumerated **19,432 session records**

Immediately before this recurrence:

- 16:53:47: enumerated 4,858 sessions
- 16:53:49: enumerated the same 4,858 sessions again

The regular Agent Service list only had **47 provider-fallback sessions**, but the Copilot prewarm enumerated the entire 4,858-session SDK store to provide metadata for those fallbacks.

### 2. Not direct metadata RPC spam

The retained AHP JSONL logs contain:

- `listSessions`: **31 actual requests**
- `getSessionMetadata`: **0**
- `sessions.getMetadata`: **0**

The current provider code deliberately performs one bulk `client.listSessions()` in `prewarmSessionMetadata`, specifically to avoid one `getSessionMetadata` RPC per session.

`AgentService` invokes that prewarm whenever even one Copilot session needs provider fallback metadata. The cache is short-lived and is cleared when that list computation finishes, so another `listSessions` call repeats the full runtime enumeration.

This is amplification rather than raw client spam: a relatively modest number of AHP list requests repeatedly caused full scans of nearly 5,000 runtime sessions.

### 3. The immediate 16:55 window also had lifecycle churn

Between 16:55 and 16:56, the logs show:

- 8 session resumes
- 8 restored sessions
- 8 disconnects
- 10 failed subscriptions to resources that had disappeared
- 20 customization-discovery failures across 16:55–16:56

So this particular recurrence appears to be:

1. Two back-to-back bulk catalog scans around 16:53:47
2. Followed by substantial resume/restore/disconnect churn around 16:55

## Live sample

The stock runtime sample captured the tail of the event:

- **126 native threads**
- **99 `copilot-cabi` threads**
- 31 `copilot-cabi` threads created or retired during the ten-second sample
- About **1.16 GB** resident memory
- CPU dropped from roughly 19% to 1% while thread count fell from 126 to 80

The sample was mostly waiting by then, with little active filesystem I/O. That is consistent with the worker pool retiring after a filesystem-heavy burst rather than an endless main-thread loop.

Raw capture: `copilot-runtime-42514-20260924-sample.txt`

## Likely fix

The most promising VS Code-side fixes are:

1. Keep the bulk SDK session metadata cache alive briefly across list computations, rather than disposing it after each pass.
2. Coalesce concurrent and trailing prewarm requests.
3. Avoid enumerating all 4,858 SDK sessions when only 47 fallback session IDs need metadata.
4. Reduce redundant local `listSessions` refreshes, especially the back-to-back pairs.

Historical context: the bulk prewarm optimization was introduced by Vijay Upadya on September 1 in [#333896](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333896), then integrated with centralized fallback metadata by Sandeep Somavarapu in [#332410](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/332410).

## tl;dr

VS Code

title: Managed enabledPlugins true does not force-enable an installed plugin
body:
## Problem

When the enterprise `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy maps an installed `plugin@marketplace` identity to `true`, the plugin is still governed by the stored user or workspace enablement choice. A user can disable it, removing its contributed hooks, skills, tools, or other customizations even though organization policy requires it.

The inverse policy value already behaves differently: a plugin mapped to `false` is disabled and cannot be re-enabled.

## Expected behavior

For plugins that are already installed and discovered:

- Managed `true` force-enables the exact `plugin@marketplace` identity.
- Managed `false` force-disables it.
- Local profile and workspace enablement writes cannot override either managed value.
- The underlying user choice is preserved and becomes effective again if the managed entry is removed.
- Plugins omitted from policy remain user-controlled; the setting stays additive rather than becoming an allowlist.
- A force-enabled plugin cannot be disabled or uninstalled through the plugin management UI.

## Verification

Configure three installed fixture plugins:

```json
{
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "required-demo@example-marketplace": true,
    "blocked-demo@example-marketplace": false
  }
}
```

Leave a third plugin omitted from policy, and pre-seed `required-demo` as locally disabled.

Verify that:

1. `required-demo` is enabled and its switch is locked.
2. `blocked-demo` is disabled and its switch is locked.
3. The omitted plugin remains user-toggleable.
4. The required plugin has no uninstall action.
5. Removing the policy entries restores the stored local choices.
6. A same-named plugin from another marketplace does not inherit the managed decision.

Fixed by #337209.

## Scope

This issue covers enablement and management controls for plugins that are already installed and discovered. Installation or restoration of a missing required plugin is tracked separately in #337221. Failure behavior when a required plugin cannot be acquired is also outside this issue.

title: Agent Host: Verify workspaceless independent session creation
body:
Allow an independent Agent Host session to be created without a workspace, even when the source session is workspace-backed.

Verification:
1. Open a workspace-backed Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent: `Create a new independent session without a workspace. Ask it to reply with workspaceless session ready.`
3. Open the created session and verify it has no selected workspace or repository.
4. Verify it did not inherit the source session folder.
5. Verify the request was delivered and the session responds.
6. Reload the Agents Window and verify the workspaceless session still appears and opens.

Implemented by #337230.

title: Agent Host: Verify configurable orchestration limits
body:
Verify the experimental `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` setting and its live process-wide limits for agent-created sessions, chats, and messages.

Verification:
1. Set `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` to `off` and start a new Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent to create enough sessions/chats or send enough messages to approach the legacy limit.
3. Verify the legacy limit is enforced with a clear error and rejected operations leave no partial session or chat.
4. Change the setting to `on` without reloading.
5. Repeat the orchestration workflow and verify the increased process-wide session, chat, and message limits apply live.
6. Verify ordinary permissions, confirmations, and input validation are unchanged.
7. Ask the agent to recursively create nested delegated work and verify spawn depth remains capped at three.
8. Toggle the setting back to `off` and verify subsequent operations use the original limits without restarting.
9. Exercise the limit from multiple active sessions and verify it is process-wide rather than scoped to one chat.
10. Verify reaching a limit does not interrupt already-running sessions.

Implemented by #337954.
